notes.title: PC Rehana Rehman | KozPure re: Downtown Dova Project Update
notes.summary_markdown:
# Project Overview and Team Introductions

- Downtown Dova Project: 7,500-seat indoor soccer arena with surrounding mixed-use development
- Site in Rancho Cordova’s Convention Overlay District; all anticipated uses permitted by right
- KozPure team introduced the full project team:
  - Charlie Tiwana: real estate development background, 15 years mixed-use/commercial
  - David Temblador: land use and environmental attorney, 26 years
  - Don Dethlefs (Perkins Will): principal architect, arena design specialist
  - Whitney Williams (Levelup-pd): owner-driven project/construction management
- Commissioner Rehana Rehman: Planning Commissioner, also an operating board member at San Juan Soccer; disclosed dual role upfront for transparency

# Site Plan and Design Strategy

- Arena positioned after hundreds of iterations; final location chosen for:
  - Back-of-house alignment with SF Market (loading stays hidden from public)
  - Pedestrian-friendly open plaza for pre/post-event activation
  - Single internal road with roundabouts (wide enough for fire engine turn radius)
  - Parking garages with 2+ entry/exit points and long queuing lanes to avoid road backup
- Distributed event parking strategy modeled on Golden 1:
  - 3/4-mile or half-mile walking radius from arena
  - Agreements with surrounding business park property owners to use vacant lots after hours
- Sewer easement under the internal road drove road placement (no buildable uses permitted above it)
- Urban mixed-use model intentional: residential density + retail + hotels encourage early arrival and late departure, dispersing traffic vs. the old “arena in a field” model

# Arena Design and Multi-Use Flexibility

- Slab-on-grade building: turf at grade level, unlike Golden 1’s buried event level
  - Loading fully hidden off north side; fenced along Trade Center Drive
- Seating: \~5,000 lower bowl + upper terrace rows = 7,500 total
  - Hospitality/premium level: suites on both sides, half-wall low suites, lofts, Club C
  - Large halo video boards inside and out
- Primary tenant: MASL (men’s and women’s indoor soccer), 85x200 ft field
- Telescopic seats retract to create 28,000 sq ft exhibit/convention floor + meeting rooms underneath
- Multi-use event configurations:
  - End-stage and center-stage concerts
  - Wrestling, MMA, boxing
  - 5 mini soccer fields, 5 volleyball courts, 12 pickleball courts, 3 NCAA basketball courts
  - Gymnastics, high school/collegiate tournaments
  - Large banquets and community events
  - High school and college graduations (noted as a community favorite in prior commissioner meetings)
- Central energy-efficient utility plant screens plaza from loading dock

# Entitlements Coming Before the Commission

- Three items before the Planning Commission next week:
  1. Major Design Review: architecture, massing, materials, site design (the primary planning question)
  2. CEQA Consistency Document: validates project impacts are consistent with prior environmental review from the general plan/convention overlay adoption; not yet published but city staff has made the determination
  3. Development Agreement (DA): 10-year term with automatic 5-year extension (15 years total) to vest land use approvals per state statute
- No conditional use permit or rezone needed; convention overlay district already permits all uses by right
- Full staff report (including \~1,000-page traffic study) to be released within \~24 hours
- Full technical team, including wet/dry utility and traffic consultants, will be present at the hearing

# Commissioner Feedback and Traffic Concerns

- Rehana expressed genuine enthusiasm for the project, especially its multifaceted programming beyond soccer
- Flagged traffic as the most consistent community concern online and on neighborhood pages:
  - Specific worry: Sunrise/Hwy 50 interchange already congested
  - Noted fellow commissioners (Lee, Dave) reliably focus on parking and traffic questions
  - Characterized community concern as fear and lack of information, not necessarily opposition
- Team’s response on traffic mitigation:
  - Urban mixed-use model meters arrival/departure times naturally
  - Distributed parking across business park disperses traffic away from a single chokepoint
- Rehana’s personal plan: review full staff report over the weekend before the special meeting
- Committed to being able to explain her vote to constituents regardless of outcome

# Next Steps

- **Review full staff report and traffic study before the Planning Commission hearing** (Rehana)

  Report drops in \~24 hours; Rehana has Friday off and plans to read through the weekend.
- **Prepare technical consultants for traffic, utilities, and CEQA questions at the hearing**

  Traffic and community concerns around Sunrise/Hwy 50 are expected to come up from multiple commissioners.
- **Make team available for any follow-up questions from Rehana before the hearing**

  KozPure offered full availability; Rehana may reach out after reviewing the documents.

---

Chat with meeting transcript: [https://notes.granola.ai/t/a9a07889-f847-45ed-a450-596ab434fa9e](https://notes.granola.ai/t/a9a07889-f847-45ed-a450-596ab434fa9e)

notes.title: PC Lee Frechette | KozPure re: Downtown Dova Project Update
notes.summary_markdown:
# Whitney’s Background (for Reference)

- Whitney and business partner Greg lead Level Up Project Development
  - Boutique owner’s rep and development management firm
  - Expertise in sports and entertainment: stadiums, training facilities, districts, racetracks
- Family relocating to the Rancho Cordova / Greater Sacramento area as the project progresses

# Commissioner Background and Role

- Commissioner Lee Frechette: engineer for the Cordova Community Council
  - Handles public infrastructure engineering: traffic counts, cell capacity, utility effluent
  - Extensive entertainment background: pyro for Super Bowl, National College Football Championship, Taylor Swift, Alice Cooper, Keith Urban; road manager for Pablo Cruz
  - Prior development experience: family development business, exited before 2008 downturn
  - Nuclear engineering master’s degree (Air Force-funded); private pilot since age 16
- Flagged upfront: will be careful about what he says or asks before the hearing

# Commissioner’s Candid Guidance on the Hearing

- Traffic will be the hardest topic for commissioners to grasp
  - Technical and easy for laypeople to glaze over
  - Biggest issue on every arena project: noise, lights, traffic, in that order, with traffic #1
- Some commissioners will ask questions outside Planning Commission scope
  - Public-private partnerships, community engagement, nonprofit support
  - References to BJ at Coreana Plaza likely to come up
  - Community Council engagement: Commissioner must stay clear of this (conflict of interest)
- Commissioner’s own stance: comfortable with entertainment and development side; will not ask about project finances (inappropriate at this stage)
- Skeptical of mode-split assumptions for a second-tier suburb
  - Practical view: people will drive; public transit uptake unlikely
  - Only real future shift: autonomous vehicles (Waymo)
- Noted: Garrett (likely a council contact) is in the same Bible study group; questions may come indirectly

# Traffic and Utilities Strategy

- \~1,000-page traffic analysis; conservative mode split taken at city and Rogers’ recommendation
- Project touches 50+ intersections in the impact area
  - Public Works Director Albert pushed for a larger study area; team credits him for holding the line
- Offsite improvements range from restriping and wayfinding to signal timing and queue management
- Sewer interceptor easement runs along the internal road; no buildings over it, road and landscaping only
  - David Temblador helped navigate sewer district approval (was chair at the time)
- Utility capacity letters secured from relevant agencies for water, sewer, and power

# Site Plan and Arena Design

- Single internal road with 2 roundabouts for slow pedestrian-friendly circulation
- 2,500 on-site parking spaces; supplemented by agreements with surrounding business park lots (vacant after 5 PM)
  - 2.8 people per vehicle at capacity: 2,500 cars aligns with 7,500-seat sellout
- Arena positioned for freeway visibility; back-of-house aligned with SF Market’s back-of-house
- Paseo pedestrian corridor lined with retail, restaurants, and coffee shops connecting all street approaches
- Residential row placed on quieter side of site; hotel locations still being finalized
- Arena design (Don Dethlefs, Perkins Will, 70 arenas):
  - Slab-on-grade, site slopes 4 feet north, ideal for loading
  - 90 ft tall; truss bottom at 70–75 ft (larger than typical 50 ft for 6,000-seat venues)
  - Lower bowl \~5,000 seats; mid-level suites, lofts, club seats; upper terrace \~6 rows
  - 6 retractable side rows + telescopic end section for concert configuration (+1,000 seats)
  - 85 × 200 ft floor: soccer, ice, indoor football, lacrosse; 28,000 sq ft trade/exhibition floor
  - Community uses: youth soccer, 5 volleyball courts, 12 pickleball courts, 3 NCAA basketball courts, banquets, gymnastics, wrestling
  - Loading: multiple tall dock doors, truck ramp directly onto arena floor, screened from Trade Center Drive
  - Central utility plant houses cooling towers, chillers, main electrical, IT
  - VIP entry separate from general public; bunker suites at event level; east-side club doubles as convention breakout space
- Fire lane on south end: dimensioned and located in coordination with Metro Fire for apparatus access

# Next Steps

- **Confirm day-of logistics for the 29th walkthrough** (Orlana)

  Don needs to know if anything requires in-person attendance before the 5:30 PM Planning Commission hearing, or if the team can fly into Sacramento that morning.
- **Share Rancho Marriott preferred rate code with Don**

  KozPure has a preferred rate arranged; code to be sent to Don's team.
- **Coordinate fly-through run-through with Mike (Don's office)** (Don)

  Mike needs to run the fly-through live in case a commissioner requests an alternate view on the 30th.
- **Align graphical language across Perkins Will and Rogers deliverables**

  Some visual dissonance noted between the two teams' materials; needs to be resolved before the hearing.

---

Chat with meeting transcript: [https://notes.granola.ai/t/ec47351f-9e78-4d8e-97ed-e4efaf6f27c7](https://notes.granola.ai/t/ec47351f-9e78-4d8e-97ed-e4efaf6f27c7)

notes.title: Zoom - Initial Slide Team Presentation for Planning Commission Hearing
notes.summary_markdown:
# Context and Background

- Planning Commission hearing scheduled for September 30th (next week)
- City Council will follow as the final decision-making body; Planning Commission is advisory only
- This presentation is a dress rehearsal: revisions expected before the Council hearing \~1 month out
- Whitney Williams and Greg Wieting (LevelUp Project Development) are owners rep/development management on the project
  - Prior experience: Mercedes-Benz Stadium (Falcons + Atlanta United), Atlanta United training facility, Jaguars training facility, Miami Freedom Park Stadium
- Team has been conducting individual pre-meetings with commissioners; those sessions have informed the slide messaging

# Slide Deck Structure and Flow

- Current deck combines Perkins \& Will slides (sent as PDF) with KozPure/Pippin slides
- Proposed presentation sequence:
  1. Master plan overview (quick orientation)
  2. Arena exterior and plaza (colored rendering)
  3. Interior bowl: flexibility, seating, video board, sightlines
  4. Event configurations: concerts, conventions, trade shows, pickleball (12 courts), volleyball, basketball (3 cross-courts), banquet (696 tables, expandable to 1,000+)
  5. Walkthrough/fly-through (in progress, upgrading from gray/B\&W to realistic renders)
  6. Traffic analysis slides (Wood Rogers/Mario)
- Interior floor plans to be held in reserve, not shown proactively unless asked
  - Commissioners have responded positively to the level of thoughtfulness and detail

# Key Messaging Priorities

- Phase 1 arena + plaza functions as a strong standalone land use
  - Site is also designed to integrate cohesively at full buildout
  - One commissioner already raised this question; get ahead of it proactively
- Future phases are concepts only: not fixed designs, subject to further revision
  - Gray out or fade non-arena portions on master plan slide to visually reinforce this
- Convention overlay district framing: emphasize breakout/meeting rooms integrated into club spaces
  - Civic “sizzle”: this venue goes beyond sports, honoring the core of the convention overlay district
- Arena square footage: confirmed at 194,110 sq ft (must stay consistent with environmental documents)
  - Central utility plant is in addition to this number
  - Approximate symbol (\~) on slide confirmed as approximate, not a minus sign

# Slide Refinements Needed

- Master plan slide: remove or white-box the legend (upper left) and square footage callouts for future phases
  - Avoid locking into specific building heights or footprints for non-Phase 1 elements
  - Rudi to send a Phase 1 boundary graphic with a clear red-line demarcation by end of day
  - Verify graphic matches what was submitted to the city (consistency with the entitlement package)
- Plaza slide: replace black-and-white drawing with the colored version; gray out non-Phase 1 areas
  - Consider a red border to delineate Phase 1 clearly
- Traffic section opening image: placeholder rendering to be swapped out
  - Current image implies full video wrap around the arena exterior; only the south side is approved
  - Tower height (\~30 stories) not yet formally discussed; flag before introducing at commission

# Traffic Analysis Slides

- Local Transportation Analysis (LTA): covers queuing and delay at Zinfandel and Sunrise interchanges
- VMT screening: project is consistent with city’s convention overlay district criteria; no detailed VMT analysis required
  - Replace “exempt” language with “consistent” throughout: sounds better and is more accurate
  - Slide should lead with “consistent with city’s convention overlay district” and stop there
- Mode split slide: shows private vehicles, rideshare, light rail, walk/bike/bus
  - Numbers are intentionally conservative, aligned with established practice and the LTA
  - SacRT condition in place; ticket-bundled transit pass expected to improve actual transit share
  - Not taking credit for that uplift in the analysis; conservative baseline protects the project
  - RT, Caltrans, and City have all been briefed; numbers should not be a surprise
- Mitigation improvements: new signals, turn lanes, queue storage, crosswalks, sidewalks, bike lanes, wayfinding (dynamic message signs), potential shuttles, event access plan
  - Consolidate all improvement locations onto one summary slide: \~40–50 intersections touched
  - Powerful rhetorical statement: “this project will be making improvements to 50 intersections”
- Matt Spokely (Wood Rogers) to present traffic section at the hearing; Mario Tambellini supporting

# Next Steps

- **Send Phase 1 boundary graphic with red-line demarcation** (Rudi)

  Must match what was submitted to the city; deliver by end of day today.
- **Update master plan slide: white-box legend and future-phase square footages**

  Avoid locking in non-Phase 1 building details; use colored version, gray out future phases.
- **Replace traffic section placeholder rendering and remove full-video-wrap implication** (Pippin)

  Video board is south side only; tower height not yet formally introduced.
- **Replace "exempt" with "consistent" on VMT slide; trim to opening sentence only** (Mario/Wood Rogers)

  Add brief filler copy for interchange sensitivity and event arrival pattern bullets for visual symmetry.
- **Build consolidated "all improvements" summary slide** (Mario/Wood Rogers)

  Combine all 4 mitigation slides into one map showing \~40–50 improvement locations.
- **Finalize walkthrough/fly-through renders before September 30th** (Don/Perkins \& Will)

  Upgrade from gray/B\&W to realistic quality; confirm path with Josh and Charlie once they're available.
- **Schedule a final slide review before September 29th** (Orlana)

  Orlana to reach out to the full team to allow time for final cleanup before the hearing.

---

Chat with meeting transcript: [https://notes.granola.ai/t/66fa8fc1-7381-4a80-9635-5870db576cd8](https://notes.granola.ai/t/66fa8fc1-7381-4a80-9635-5870db576cd8)

notes.title: Cordova Arena | Level Up + Jones Discussion
notes.summary_markdown:
# Jones Company Overview

- Headquarters in Green Bay; historically known for signage and architectural metals
- Now pursuing aggressive growth beyond signage: architectural fabrication, LED systems, canopy structures, exterior metal panels
- 300,000 sq ft steel shop in Green Bay with 3 CNC machines
- In-house LED capability: direct relationships with YAHAM and LG, full install and commissioning
- Active projects: $14M ACM job at Houston International Airport, Kalamazoo Event Center ($9M), Nissan Stadium (grew from $3M to $7-9M), Hard Rock Casino Vegas LED curtain wall
- Pursuing: Rays stadium, Cincinnati Bengals
- Notable past work: FC Cincinnati facade, [Lower.com](http://Lower.com) Field perforated metal panel, Wells Fargo Center LED retrofit, Climate Pledge Arena rooftop (helicopter lift), Orlando City naming rights (5-6 week turnaround), LA Dodgers field-level signage
- Placemaking highlight: NFL Hall of Fame Centennial Plaza in Canton, Ohio
  - 60-ft stainless steel spires, lattice canopy structure, full LED, all turnkey by Jones

# Cordova Arena Project Status

- 7,500-seat fully indoor arena in Rancho Cordova
- Tenants: men’s and women’s arena soccer, ice hockey, Sac State basketball and volleyball conversations
- Programming goal: 365-day flexible use, concerts, Disney on Ice, MMA
- Owner: CosPure (Josh and Charlie), first major project
  - Josh: Sacramento roots, politics and lobbying background, helped with Golden 1 Arena
  - Charlie: development background, city council experience
- Privately developed with significant public involvement
  - Tax revenue agreement, land transfer, and city council hearings in progress
- Strong city and community support; building department actively expediting reviews

# Design and Schedule Milestones

- AOR: Perkins and Will; structural: Beugler Martin; food service consultants in place
- Design kickoff with Perkins and Will happened last week
- Key schedule dates:
  - 50% SDs: 10/16
  - 100% SDs: 11/20

notes.title: DOVA Design Team Coordination
notes.summary_markdown:
# Meeting Purpose and Milestones

- Coordinate Schematic Design activities, resolve cross-discipline issues, and maintain information flow for SD and Site Development Plan submission
- Upcoming milestones: 
  - Week 3: Owner meeting
  - 9/30: City (Planning Commission) meeting
  - Week 5: 50% SD check set
- BIM model access: confirm all team members have access; contact Brian at Perkins Will if not
- Contact list: fill out ASAP and identify BIM lead

# Owner and Contractor Updates

- NVAC relocation confirmed: Josh and Charlie approved moving it from current position 
  - Whitney to coordinate with Chuck and Rudy on new location
  - Intent: run infrastructure and cap it even if Phase 1 building isn’t built out
- SkyGrid roof feature: not a Phase 1 requirement; feasibility study needed; “Day 2 ready”
- CM bidder outreach: RFI sent to Suffolk, Level 10, and AECOM Hunt asking for concrete vs. steel vs. hybrid preference 
  - Responses requested by 10/2; Suffolk (Will Gamba) informally recommends concrete to concourse level, steel rakers above
  - All three confirmed interest; responses will be distributed to the full team
- Light RFP planned: Whitney to share draft with Don for alignment before issuing 
  - Exhibit package to include: geotech, civil, 50% SDs, program narrative
  - Template response form for apples-to-apples comparison (inclusions, exclusions, qualifications)
  - Goal: contractor on board by start of DD phase
  - Don noted AI renderings from the 9/30 meeting can be included in the RFP package

# 9/30 Planning Commission Meeting

- Fly-through will open with the existing rendering (commissioners have seen it for months), then transition into the lobby interior
- Exterior model will not be updated before the 30th; white-box exterior will not be shown
- Parallel in-house effort underway to evaluate a simplified exterior design (Kyle at Perkins Will, coordinating with Simon in SF) 
  - Goal: simpler, more cost-effective alternative to the current all-glass triangular column facade
  - No more than two options to present; must not cost more
  - Josh and Charlie will decide after the 30th whether to evolve the look

# Site Civil Coordination

- Mass grading scope under discussion: may be limited to Phase 1 area only (vs. full site) due to environmental fees 
  - Wood Rogers evaluating grade balance implications given the site slopes north
- Satellite and studio truck access: trucks entering via Sunrise interchange, right onto Trade Center Drive, left into complex 
  - City required offsite improvements to accommodate this route (previous circuitous route denied)
  - Loading dock angle likely needs adjustment: trucks were designed assuming east entry, not west
  - Wood Rogers to share turning templates with the full team
- Satellite truck sightlines: Mark (WJHW) to research required view angle and dish clearance; satellite trucks need line of sight, studio trucks do not 
  - Studio trucks: 54-ft trailers, double expando (effectively twice standard width); cabs often dropped on-site
- NVAC removal reopens opportunity for \~20-space secured player/staff parking in the northeast area; loading dock layout to be revisited holistically
- Central Utility Plant (CUP): discussion on pulling it back 30–40 ft to reduce visual impact on south/southeast corner 
  - JCI requires continuous access doors along northeast face (flush, paved)
  - Must still accommodate: emergency generator, 2 transformers, future exterior ice chiller (\~40 ft long)
  - Triangular space between CUP and oval to be resolved once turning templates are reviewed
- Telecom/ISP infrastructure: handholes and manhole locations around the arena to be coordinated collectively by the full team (not a separate scope)
- Fire lane: fire department requires parallel access to 50% of building roof circumference; explains current fire lane geometry

# Structural Approach

- Leaning toward concrete base to concourse level (possibly suite level), steel above and for rakers 
  - Primary driver: schedule, not cost; concrete saves 3–4 months vs. steel saving \~$3–4M but adding 6–8 months
  - Precast expected to be the recommendation; SPS has hidden costs
  - Buehler to provide concept-level quantities (concrete mass, reinforcement, steel tonnage) to support pricing
  - Don does not expect any contractor to recommend full-height concrete given California labor costs
- Structural loads still needed from other disciplines: halo/LED, ribbon boards, exterior displays, RTUs, rigging, solar

# Roof Plan and MEP Coordination

- Roof plan options under study to create more mechanical equipment space: 
  - Option A: flatten north and/or south sides of oval roof (gains \~5 ft per side)
  - Option B: extend south truss to building edge, creating a dedicated mechanical roof zone
  - Chad (ME Engineers) prefers opening the south zone; would place 2 bowl units there, freeing east-west wings for AHUs serving locker rooms and kitchen exhaust
  - South lobby likely needs a dedicated unit due to significant glass and limited overhang
- Structural note: pulling back the south truss could facilitate shear transfer from high to low roof
- JCI CUP coordination meeting needed: Whitney to set up with Wood Rogers, ME Engineers, and JCI to confirm CUP scope and contents
- Food service coordination meeting scheduled for 9/25

# Video Board (Halo Board) Design

- i5 LED meeting debrief: owner (Josh and Charlie) consider the current halo board too small; want it larger
- Key constraints: 
  - Video board cannot be in the “gray zone” below the stage rigging area
  - Should not come within 15 ft of the front of the stage (Mark: 10–15 ft for sound; lighting TBC)
  - Sports lighting at 45-degree angle from center ice/turf is largely blocked by the larger board
  - Board cannot tilt vertically (cost-prohibitive)
- Three height options under review: 
  1. Reduce board depth (keeps truss, raises board slightly)
  2. Reduce truss depth (pulls board up without raising roof)
  3. Raise the roof (adds cost; least preferred)
- Shape options: fat oval vs. racetrack (straight sides, curved corners); team leans toward keeping oval
- Board width: may need to get shorter longitudinally but wider laterally to stay impressive while clearing rigging
- Separate meeting needed with George Reiher (ME Engineers) to work through sports lighting and halo board integration 
  - Chad to relay to George; Don to send cross-sections and longitudinal sections to ME team
- Future-proofing: design to accommodate potential full bottom-of-truss video board (SkyNet ceiling) as a Day 2 addition
- Video content ratio: reducing board height shortens the 16 in a 9:16 ratio; i5 confirmed panels can be configured flexibly within \~1 ft

# Week 3 Look Ahead and Next Steps

- Architecture: site/landscape/architecture review, catwalk plan, roof plan, acoustic approach
- Civil + MEP: flow/fixture-unit estimate for SDP
- Structural: building maintenance plan meeting/coordination
- AV: acoustic approach
- Owner: solar confirmation, confirm responsibility for site lighting
- Team: prepare for 9/30 City meeting
- Live model/drawing site: Sam to pull together a shared live repository; in the meantime, Don/Mike to email latest halo board drawing and sections to full team

## Original Agenda Topics Not Reached

- **Architecture + Structural:** review the current structural grid and column placement; schedule an Architecture/Structural meeting to review the initial analysis; confirm structural loads for exterior wall systems, RTUs/mechanical equipment, rigging, and solar.
- **MEP:** confirm the fire pump room requirements and location; identify MEP room or shaft requirements affecting the architectural plans; advance preliminary AHU locations using the roof plan.
- **AV / Technology / Arena Systems:** confirm LED scope for halo, ribbon boards, and exterior board; determine remaining i5LED needs; identify AV/technology infrastructure affecting the site or major building spaces, including control room size; look ahead to the Week 3 acoustic approach.
- **Food Service:** continue preliminary planning, including arena kitchen precedent information, kitchen/concession locations, and grease waste, gas, exhaust, and utility implications; coordination meeting is scheduled for 9/25.
- **Week 3 readiness:** complete the planned Site/Landscape/Architecture review, catwalk plan, roof plan, acoustic approach, Civil + MEP flow/fixture-unit estimate for the SDP, Structural building-maintenance-plan coordination, AV acoustic approach, owner solar confirmation and site-lighting responsibility, and team preparation for the 9/30 City meeting.
- **Decisions, Actions + Next Steps:** review new decisions, identify risks/information requests, and confirm focused coordination meetings needed during the week.

# Next Steps

- **Coordinate NVAC relocation with Chuck and Rudy** (Whitney)
- **Share draft light RFP with Don for alignment** (Whitney)
- **Distribute CM bidder responses to full team after 2nd October** (Whitney)
- **Share truck turning templates with the design team** (Matt Spokely)
- **Research satellite truck sightline requirements and dish clearance** (Mark Graham)
- **Set up CUP coordination meeting with Wood Rogers, ME Engineers, and JCI** (Whitney)
- **Schedule separate video board/sports lighting meeting with George Reiher**
- **Schedule i5 LED meeting before SMUD meeting** (Whitney)
- **Email latest halo board drawings and sections to full team** (Don, Mike)

---

notes.title: PC Dave Huhn | KozPure re: Downtown Dova Project Update
notes.summary_markdown:
# Attendees and Context

- Planning Commission pre-meeting briefing ahead of the September 30th hearing
- Commissioner Dave Huhn (Rancho Cordova Planning Commission) hosted by KozPure team
- KozPure principals: Josh Wood, Charlie Tiwana, Orlana Van Zandt
- Design team: Don Dethlefs and Sam Kalscheur (Perkins Will, 70+ arenas)
- Land use attorney: David Temblador (26 years, land use and environmental)
- Owner’s rep: Whitney Williams (Level Up), specializing in sports and entertainment

# Entitlement Package Overview

- Hearing date: September 30th
- Primary entitlement: Major Design Review (MDR), discretionary but not a land use question
  - All uses permitted by right within the city’s Convention Overlay District
  - Prior council approvals and existing environmental documents already in place
- CEQA: conformance document in progress; city has confirmed consistency determination
- Three-part agreement structure:
  1. Development Agreement: 10-year term + 5-year extension (15-year total horizon)
  2. Financial Participation Agreement: tax share, CFDs, economic incentives (city council, not planning commission)
  3. Land Transfer Agreement: city parcel assemblage component (city council)
- Commissioner Dave Huhn will not attend the September 30th hearing (prior commitment: Repcore golf event at Old Greenwood, Truckee)

# Arena Design and Configuration

- 7,500-seat multipurpose arena, slab-on-grade (above grade, no bowl excavation)
  - Avoids dewatering issues that plagued Golden 1’s deep bowl
- Located at the north end of the development, with a “Main Street” (Tiwana Passage) aimed at the south-facing main entries
- Five entry points on the south side; loading and service on the north, hidden from Trade Center Drive
- Three seating levels:
  - Lower bowl: designed around 85x200 ft turf (arena soccer, football, lacrosse, ice events, circus)
  - Hospitality suite/club level: suites on both sides, loges and specialty seating
  - Upper terrace: 5-6 open rows per side with 360-degree concourse view
- Concert configuration: telescopic end seats retract to reveal stage; maximizes capacity and affordability
- Expanded floor mode: 6 retractable rows per side open floor to 120 ft across
  - Enables rodeo, motocross, MMA, GA floor, banquet (28,000 sq ft exhibition floor)
- Multi-use event configurations demonstrated: MASL soccer, volleyball (5 courts), pickleball, basketball (3 courts), banquet
- Ice-ready design: infrastructure provision for future chiller and Zamboni; no ice tenant yet
- Large halo board, ribbon boards, and dasher boards planned throughout

# Infrastructure and Utilities

- Water: coordinating with Golden State Water; well-served
- Power: working with SMUD on usage and capacity; confirmed ability to serve the arena
- Central Utility Plant (CUP): designed to expand for district heating/cooling for future hotel and residential phases
  - JCI (Johnson Controls) leading the CUP component
- Parking strategy: distributed across existing business park lots within walking distance, similar to Golden 1 model
  - Several agreements already in place with property owners
  - Access from Highway 50, Sunrise, and Folsom Boulevard
- Transit: coordinating with Sac RT (light rail) and Sac Metro Fire
  - Fire access confirmed from two points: Trade Center Drive and the on-site plaza road

# Commissioner’s Ideas and Feedback

- Skybridge concept: 5-story parking garage across Trade Center Drive with a 3rd-level skybridge into the plaza
  - Top 2 floors reserved as a Waymo autonomous vehicle hub; lower 3 for general parking
  - During events, Waymos relocate autonomously, freeing all 5 levels for event parking
  - Bridge doubles as signage/advertising and a pedestrian safety feature
- Traffic concern: Kilgore, Trade Center, and Sunrise Boulevard need capacity upgrades before opening
  - Suggested widening Kilgore and improving the Kilgore-Folsom-Trade Center block
- Infrastructure priorities flagged: fire safety, water, sewer, power, and traffic management
- Enthusiastic about the design; compared arena shape favorably to the Colosseum
- Community sentiment: residents excited about the project; primary concern is traffic

# Mixed-Use Development and Phasing

- Phase 1: arena + event plaza + green space (active outdoor lawn for events)
  - Two small plaza buildings to follow in a later phase
- Full buildout: \~10 years; includes 1,000 parking spaces on-site and 1,000 residential units across 4 buildings
- Hotels, retail, meeting spaces, movie theaters also planned within the district
- Construction phased to allow events to continue while other components are built
- Arena and plaza estimated at 18-20 months to build

# Design Team and Next Steps

- Full design team:
  - Perkins Will: architecture (Don Dethlefs, Sam Kalscheur)
  - WJHW: acoustics/AV
  - i5: large video boards (local)
  - Wood Rogers: civil engineering and landscape/plaza design (local)
  - JCI: central utility plant and controls
- Commissioner keen to reconvene after the September 30th hearing for further discussion
- PowerPoint deck not shareable per city rules; will be made available once public
- Dave Huhn attending September 30th hearing remotely not feasible; will participate after the fact

# Next Steps

- **Address Commissioner's infrastructure questions before the September 30th hearing** (David Temblador)

  Dave Huhn flagged traffic, sewer, water, and power capacity as key concerns; team committed to providing feedback ahead of the hearing.
- **Schedule follow-up meeting with Commissioner Huhn post-hearing**

  Dave Huhn requested a sit-down after the September 30th commission meeting to walk through design ideas in more depth.

---

Chat with meeting transcript: [https://notes.granola.ai/t/2b404dd2-d144-4bd5-b9bc-120057b4e173](https://notes.granola.ai/t/2b404dd2-d144-4bd5-b9bc-120057b4e173)

notes.summary_markdown:
# Epic Brokers Team Intro

- Mary Grandy: broker placing the project, long relationship with Josh
- Scott Brama: 8 years at Epic, 23+ years in construction insurance and risk management
- Hugh Coyle: 35 years in the business, specializes in OSIPs, CSIPs, and project-specific placements
  - Handled $35-40B in projects, delivered hundreds of millions in claims
  - Notable: came second on Millennium Tower, later brought back to consult on the fix

# Project Status: Inter Miami and Sacramento Arena

- LevelUp engaged since April 2024 on Inter Miami Stadium; now transitioning focus to Sacramento (Dova)
- Design team: Perkins Will (architect of record), Wood Rogers (civil), ME Engineers (MEP), WHW (AV), Buhler + Martin Martin (structural)
- SDs wrapping up now; 50% SD set issues October 16th
- Key permitting milestones:
  - Sacramento Planning Commission hearing: September 30th
  - City Council hearings: October 26th and November 2nd (major design review + development agreement)
- Target groundbreaking: January 2027, pending cultural clearances and site plan approval
  - Wet season in Northern California flagged as a scheduling consideration
- Contractor RFP process:
  - Full RFP issued week of October 20th (after SD set)
  - 3-4 week response window; target contractor selection mid-to-late November
  - Goal: LNTP signed heading into DDs by end of November
  - Shortlist: AECOM Hunt, Level 10 (contact: John Asunto), Suffolk
  - All three aware of OSIP program; asked to provide points and rates

# Insurance Program and Next Steps

- Epic presented a four-pillar project risk framework:
  1. OSIP (general liability)
  2. Builder’s risk (fire, windstorm, hail, earthquake, flood)
  3. Pollution legal liability / CPL (for dirty dirt, USTs, mold)
  4. Owner’s protective liability (sits atop A/E and other professionals’ coverage)
- Too early for a formal quote; need more data before going to market
  - Josh pressing for numbers, but team aligned that information gathering comes first
- Epic to send data point checklist to develop a pro forma (hard cost, soft cost, project term)
  - Whitney to fill in budget figures with appropriate caveats for a preliminary indication
- Epic to resend OSIP exhibit to Whitney directly
- Onkar to be looped in by Whitney when appropriate; Epic will communicate through Whitney for now

# Next Steps

- **Share master budget data points with Epic** (Whitney)

  Epic will send a checklist; Whitney to fill in figures with caveats to develop a preliminary pro forma indication.
- **Resend OSIP exhibit and team contact sheet to Whitney** (Mary)

  Whitney did not receive the original; Mary to resend directly to Whitney only.
- **Share contractor OSIP points and rates with Epic as they come in** (Whitney)

  Hunt, Level 10, and Suffolk are all providing terms; sharing will help Epic benchmark the program.
- **Loop Epic in on RFP insurance language before issuing** (Whitney)

  Epic offered to review contractual indemnification language and any CSIP vs. OSIP commentary from contractors.

  - City Council (not Planning Commission) will be the approval authority for design review; Planning Commission issues a recommendation only
  - City Council will approve: design review, conditions of approval, CEQA 15183 exemption, tax sharing agreement, land transfer agreement, and first reading of the Development Agreement
  - Second City Council hearing approves the Development Agreement
  - City Council dates: 10/26 and 11/2
- Planning Commission call with commissioner went well; he was pro-arena, focused on infrastructure (power, water); raised data center concerns as a proxy for community questions
- City Council slides: Whitney’s Level Up deck (intro, PM approach, cost/schedule strategy, CM procurement) submitted to Elena; 2 schedule slides included (macro + detailed); open to tweaks
- Key upcoming dates:
  1. 9/28: internal slide walkthrough
  2. 9/30: Planning Commission hearing
  3. 10/1: Premium offerings/club and suite spaces review (1 PM)
  4. 10/16: 50% SD
  5. 10/26 + 11/2: City Council (land transfer, revenue agreements, DA)
  6. 11/20: 100% SD; CM pricing; groundbreaking target January 2027
- Whitney in Sacramento 9/28-10/1 (flies in Monday night); Greg back from Japan (14 days: Tokyo then Kyoto) Friday, also plans to be in Sacramento next week

# Next Steps

- **Scrub JCI budget and prep internal position before joint meeting** (Whitney)

  Confirm what true incremental scope justifies the $55M-to-$76M jump; identify target numbers to bring JCI back to.
- **Confirm Hunt resource allocation for this project** (Whitney)

  Ask Tony and Corey directly whether West Coast team resources are shifting to the Chiefs job.

notes.summary_markdown:
# Purpose and Scope Alignment

- Goal: align LED design scope, integration points, and cross-discipline coordination across i5, ME, WJHW, and structural teams
- SD phase now formally underway; design team (including Campbell and consultants) re-kicked off last Thursday
- Working toward 50% then 100% SD; LED package drives electrical, AV, and structural decisions

# Current i5 LED Scope

- Ceiling LED (SkyGrid) removed from current scope
  - Whitney to confirm with Costco today; adding it back does not resolve the underlying issues
  - Question remains: design building to be SkyGrid-ready for future addition?
- Active scope includes:
  - Halo board (size still TBD: original smaller vs. larger)
  - Exterior board (scale TBD)
  - Ribbon LED throughout building
  - Dasher/pitch boards (terminology varies; same boards convert ice-to-turf)
- i5 package covers: LED panels, display structure, and estimated rough structural support
- Excluded from i5 scope:
  - Ancillary support steel
  - Content management, video control systems, and software
  - Fiber, conduit, and cabling (expected to be in place before i5 arrives)

# Design Scope Delineation

- Handoff points flagged as a key gray area; formal delineation matrix needed
  - Matrix to cover: display, device power, data, cabling, MEP/infrastructure, and construction
  - WJHW handles cabling and fiber design up to the rack; rack location (catwalk behind exterior board) confirmed
  - ME and structural not on this call; separate session needed to close gaps
- i5 glass-embedded LED raised as option for elevators and railings
  - Josh and Charlie reacted positively; aligns with their stated vision for activating the elevator
  - Physical mockup recommended before any commitment; i5 to bring Josh and Charlie to see glass railing in person

# Halo Board Design Challenges

- Halo board size and position unresolved; several competing constraints:
  - Sightlines: bottom of board currently drops below upper terrace level at \~22–23 ft truss height
  - Sports lighting: floodlights risk washing out the outside of the board; lights above the board blind lower-bowl fans looking up
  - Concert staging: a large dead-hung board over the end stage (10–15 ft clearance zone for lights and sound) is a major conflict
- Shape options discussed:
  - Pure oval: viewing angle poor at ends; flattening the ends (closer to Intuit Dome model) improves 16:9 replay viewing
  - Racetrack (straightaways with curved corners): better for stage clearance; angled panels on straightaways are feasible
  - Angled/triangular cross-section: dramatically increases cost; oval + angle combination ruled out as unaffordable
- Halo board servicing:
  - Lowering via winches is preferred (cleaning required annually; Bosun’s chair access is more expensive and difficult)
  - Winches are not included in current i5 pricing; would be an add
  - 6 rows of telescopic seating retract to give 120 ft clear floor for lowering
- Halo-as-SkyGrid concept floated:
  - Hinge the racetrack board up flat to the truss bottom for concerts; it becomes the ceiling board
  - Mechanically complex and pixel pitch/weight constraints are a concern
- Next modeling step: Perkins Will to develop options comparing oval (flattened), racetrack, and hinged configurations

  Call already on Whitney's agenda today; confirm current scope and whether future SkyGrid-readiness is required.
- **Raise SkyGrid-readiness question with Josh and Charlie**

  Determine whether the building should be designed to accommodate a future horizontal ceiling board.
- **Model Halo board shape options** (Don, Sam)

  Develop and compare oval (flattened), racetrack, and hinged configurations against sightline, lighting, and concert staging constraints.
- **Schedule fly-through with i5 to review current Revit model**

  i5 needs to see the latest design to make firm recommendations on board sizing and placement.
- **Arrange i5 glass railing mockup visit**

  Josh, Charlie, and relevant design team members to visit i5 facility to see glass-embedded LED in person before committing.

  Map every handoff point across display, power, data, cabling, MEP, and construction to eliminate gaps and duplication between i5, ME, WJHW, and structural.

notes.title: FW: NHS6 - Weekly Enclosure Coordination
notes.summary_markdown:
# Enclosure System Study (Buro Happold Matrix)

- 30-page preliminary enclosure study issued: good/better/best matrix across system strategy, construction, building envelope performance
- Key stakeholders needed to review the matrix were not on the call
- Next step: Sphere team reviews, compiles questions, brings them to the Sept 29 call
- Josh to send a summary email framing what decisions are needed and what questions to bring back

# October 2nd Structural Deadline (Severud)

- Severud needs facade enclosure direction by Oct 2 to finalize foundation design
- Core question: precast vs. unitized panels, as load differences are substantial
- John’s recommendation: confirm panel weight assumptions by Oct 2 rather than committing to a full system
  - Precast weight was held from Concept Plus; prefer to hold the conservative number until further clarity
  - Mega panel options may still carry significant steel backup, so not simply 50% lighter
- Josh to connect Buro Happold with Severud this week to align on what weight they’ve been designing to

# Procurement and Gate 1 Schedule

- Foundation permit package targets Nov 16; Gate 1 exterior envelope targets Nov 18
- These two packages are effectively issuing simultaneously, not 5 weeks apart as previously stated
- Sphere and Severud are running on different schedule tracks: TVS to reconcile
- Procurement package requires a real system decision by that date; TVS needs to start drawing wall sections and specs soon

# Facade System Options and Rainscreen Question

- Three systems under consideration: precast, IMP (metal panel), unitized hybrid
  - Options 1 and 2 are surface-barrier systems (sealant-reliant)
  - Option 3 is the only true rainscreen
- Concept Plus specified precast plus metal panel scrim wall, creating a double-wall assembly
  - Construction team has flagged this as slow and costly
  - Unclear who directed Manica to pursue the metal panel over precast route
- Key open question: does the project require a double wall/drainage plane, or can it depart from Concept Plus?
  - Josh to include this as an explicit question in the summary email to the Sphere team

# Acoustics and Vanguardia

- Acoustic performance is a critical factor in system selection
  - Concept Plus acoustic summary states concrete mass is required
  - Metal panel schemes may conflict with this requirement; precast provides mass, panels require added insulation
  - Warranty issue: precast manufacturer will not warrant a metal panel attached to their system
- Two acoustic goals: keep interior noise in, keep exterior noise (e.g., aircraft) out; different frequency strategies may apply
- Josh to set up a call with Vanguardia this week so they can review the 3 options and weigh in before the Sept 29 call
  - Vincent flagged HoloPlot implications: Vanguardia should also address material reflections and beamforming

# Roof Assembly

- Vegas spray-applied roof not recommended for National Harbor
  - NH has far more mechanical equipment, higher foot traffic, freeze-thaw, rain, snow, and ice
  - Vegas roof already showing wear where people walk; no serviceable equipment on Vegas roof vs. hundreds of pounds of modules at NH
- Two proposed zones for NH roof:
  - Dome/curved surface: spray polyurethane on concrete deck (waterproofing from day one), then spray foam insulation, then second polyurethane coat
    - \~10–20% more expensive than Vegas approach; durability is the value
  - Flat roof: conventional system with vapor barrier, tapered insulation, coverboard, cold-applied PMMA/polyurethane membrane, and walkway pads
- Hybrid zoning (conventional only near mechanical units, Vegas-style elsewhere) discussed but not recommended: creates patchwork, confusion over walkable vs. non-walkable zones
- No SRI code requirement in this jurisdiction: roof color can be driven by project aesthetics
- Roofing slides to be issued today; design note to follow as Part 2
- Green roof system flagged as likely to be value-engineered out

# Ice, Snow, and Energy Code

- Ice and snow mitigation flagged as an ongoing concern, particularly at secondary entries
  - Heat tracing the full exosphere is not feasible
  - Main entrance has a canopy; other VIP/secondary entries currently lack adequate protection
  - If canopies are needed, steel is already the first package out: design decisions must happen quickly
  - Cost add will need to be presented to the Sphere team as a formal decision point
- Energy model confirmed: ME is running a full energy model, so prescriptive COMcheck for enclosure components is not required
  - COMcheck is the last permit submitted; Emery flagged it can bite late if not tracked

# Next Steps

- **Send summary email to Sphere team with decision requests and updated slides** (Josh)

  Cover system weights for Severud by Oct 2, procurement decisions by Nov 16–18, and the double-wall/rainscreen clarification question.
- **Connect Buro Happold with Severud this week** (Josh)

  Align on what panel weight Severud has been designing to since Concept Plus.
- **Set up call with Vanguardia this week** (Josh)

  Give them the week to review the 3 facade options before the Sept 29 call; include HoloPlot/beamforming implications per Vincent.
- **Send updated roof and facade slides to Josh within 1–2 hours** (John)

  Josh will attach to the summary email as supplemental material to the package already distributed.
- **Align with Emery on schedule before sending summary email** (Josh)

  Ensure targeted decision deadlines are included so the Sphere team understands the constraints.
- **Review updated slides with Dan Gray on Friday morning** (Emery)

  Force a review of the most current package ahead of the Sept 29 call.

---

# Wind Pit Floor Cavity: Finishes and Structure

- Floor cavity is one large space, to be filled with structure post-construction
- Outlet hatch lid: solid steel plate; inlet hatch lids: steel or aluminum (TBD, weight study in progress)
- Infill sections between hatches: likely steel plate
- Floor finish color: matte black for prototype
  - Basalt gray (current epoxy) being reconsidered
  - Reflectivity and light bleed studies still needed before final decision
  - Black flagged as showing stains and scratches more than gray
- David N. (TVS) to add floor finish of bowl to the open items list

# Pit Access, Drainage, and Maintenance

- Pit cavity is 12 ft deep in S6 venue, not full standing height under fans
- Ship’s ladder preferred over full stair for access; telehandler needed for heavy plate removal
- Access hatch at GA floor level (house left/right, near BFT area) proposed for lifting materials
  - Bolt-down, no fancy hatch required; sized for VFD swap-out clearance
- Preference: all access from inside the bowl, not via tunnel to stage box
  - Stage box corridor eats space and cost, escalates quickly
  - Single access point likely sufficient; code review needed on confined space classification
- Tait has not yet designed the ship’s ladder or above-grade access hatch: scope to be confirmed

notes.title: PC Elliott Stevenson | KozPure re: Downtown Dova Project Update
notes.summary_markdown:
# Project Overview and Entitlement Status

- 28-acre mixed-use development anchored by a 7,500-seat arena (Phase 1)
- Buy-right project under the Convention Overlay District
  - All uses pre-approved; planning director confirmed arena as a consistent buy-right use
  - Sole discretionary action required: major design review
  - Development agreement also coming before the commission
    - 10-year initial term, 5-year extension if project proceeds on schedule
    - City requests exclusion of uses incompatible with the DOVA district vision
- Additional agreements (not before Planning Commission):
  - Revenue participation agreement and land transfer go to City Council
  - City Council previously adopted an EDPA (Economic Development Participation Agreement) as the framework
- Planning Commission hearing: September 30th
- City Council final action: October 26th

# Arena Design and Site Plan

- Slab-on-grade building; event/playing surface at ground level
  - Escalators, stairs, and elevators up to concourse, suite, and upper levels
  - Main entries on south side connecting to mixed-use district and parking
  - North side: screened loading area for concerts and sporting events
- Flexible playing surface: 85x200 ft for soccer, converts for basketball, wrestling, trade shows, large tournaments
  - Telescopic seating throughout; upper telescopic section retracts for stage events, adding \~1,000 concert capacity
- Premium amenities: cabana seats, endline and side clubs, bunker suites, loge and loft seating
- Central utility plant on site
- Two anchor sports teams: men’s and women’s soccer; building designed for broad community use
- Don Dethlefs (Perkins Will) noted this is his 70th arena

# Phase 2 and Full District Vision

- Full 28-acre build-out target: within 10 years
- Phase 2 components (architect selection in progress):
  - Hotels flanking the plaza (noise buffer for events)
  - \~1,000 residential units (mix of rental and condo; pricing not yet finalized)
  - Retail, restaurants, movie theater, parking garages
  - Miniature golf atop parking garage; outdoor spaces for pop-up events
- Pedestrian-focused design: walkable central passageway lined with restaurants and retail leading to arena
- \~2,500 parking spaces on site; all lots with at least 2 entry/exit points
- Two transit stops nearby; designed as transit-oriented development
- Day-to-day retail (grocers, pharmacy/drugstore) explicitly included after lessons learned from Sacramento development
  - Elliott raised the pharmacy/convenience store need; team confirmed it’s within approved uses

# CEQA and Regulatory Coordination

- CEQA streamlining via 15-183 conforming document (project consistent with previously adopted plan)
  - Primary focus of environmental review: traffic and circulation
- Coordination completed with Metro Fire, regional agencies on life safety and access
- Final conditions from city in hand; strong staff recommendation expected for the 30th
- Meeting later same day with city manager and city attorney to finalize development agreement details

# Next Steps

- **Attend Planning Commission hearing on 30th September**

  Major design review and development agreement up for action; strong staff recommendation anticipated.
- **Monitor City Council final action on 26th October**

  Revenue participation agreement, land transfer, design review, and development agreement all go to council together.

---

notes.title: Level Up + L&S Intro
notes.summary_markdown:
# Lang Schwander Overview

- FF\&E procurement and manufacturing firm, \~18 years in business
- Direct-source model: custom manufacturing through global factory relationships, in-house engineers and architects for shop drawings
- Approved preferred procurement consultant for Marriott, IHG, Hyatt, Choice, and others
- Services offered à la carte: manufacturing, shipping, logistics, install, punch listing
- Primary focus on upscale/luxury, but capable of mid-scale; active in US, Caribbean, Latin America

# Pricing and Fee Structure

- Two models:
  - Custom manufacturing: margin built into product cost, no additional fees; most cost-efficient option
  - Classical procurement: flat fee as a percentage of product value, acting as procurement agent only
- Shop drawings included and become client’s intellectual property
- QA team embedded in factories with progress updates throughout production

# Dove Arena Project Overview

- 7,500-seat indoor, conditioned arena in Sacramento; mixed-use entertainment district anchor
- Primary tenant: arena soccer (men’s and women’s); flexible for basketball, ice, concerts, martial arts, corporate events
- District to include 2 hotels, residential, office, movie theater, retail
- Schematic design just kicked off; SD phase completes \~November 20th
- Groundbreaking target: Q1 2027; 18-month build targeting Q2/Q3 2028 completion
- Hotels phased after the arena; flag not yet identified; Perkins Will likely Architect of Record

# FF\&E Process and Fit

- Procurement engagement planned for DD/CD phase, once furniture plan is fleshed out with architect
- Process: collect department wish lists (operations, sporting teams), specify fixed furniture via interior plan, pull comparison options (spec match, value alternative, budget option)
- High-end/premium spaces: sample reviews, seat tests, dog-and-pony show for ownership selections
- Long-lead items purchased early; escrow fund set up for staged payments
- Lang Schwander noted stadium FF\&E is new territory for them, but suites and clubs mirror hotel-grade furniture

# Next Steps

- SD package to be shared around November 20th to begin building FF\&E budgets
- Lang Schwander to follow up end of November if no contact by then


- **Share SD drawings with Lang Schwander around 20th November** (Whitney)

  Trigger point to begin building out FF\&E budgets for Dove Arena.
- **Visit Hyatt Centric on Collins Ave with Lang Schwander** (Whitney)

  Brian offered a site tour to showcase their product quality before any contract commitment.
- **Pass Lang Schwander contact details to the Kozpure team** (Whitney)

  Josh and Charlie's team also has hotels and office buildings that could be a fit.

---

  - Ownership strategy: hold payment as leverage for better settlement terms
  - Counter-argument: staff campus has active mold problem, needs urgent remediation

- Kroll’s current potential recovery estimate for Alpha Insulation: \~$45K
- $235K not yet moved to “potentially recoverable” column; needs to be echoed over

- Alpha Video: scope complete, $436K sales tax credit provided; working directly with Ricky on additional items outside contract

  - \~10–15 locations with damaged glass still to fix
  - Withholding payment blocking pricing of CO items (sharp edges on railings, west stack glass railing height)
  - Using Mr. Glass instead would cost \~3x more vs. Alpha Cladding (shoe vs. full glass replacement)
- AIS: essentially complete except retainage; straightforward payment

# Convergent: Cameras, Access Control, and Closeout

- \~7 cameras not installed by Convergent; MassTech installing using Convergent-supplied cameras

- Access control credentials dispute resolved; MassTech now using operations login
  - Access control system still not fully operational; MassTech working to bring it online
- Graham wants to pursue a quick settlement with a discount to close Convergent out

- DCL has been vocal, reaching out weekly
- East ribbon change order: reduced from \~$181K down to \~$50K; revised submission already in Procore
- Additional reduction on East Club work: from $186K down to $49K
- One further reduction pending; Whitney to follow up with DCL
- Outstanding balance: \~$2.2M; \~$1M+ still remaining under contract
- Strategy: gather full information on disputed items, then offer partial payment (\~$1.5M) as start of a settlement targeting \~$1M deduct
- Procore invoicing may not be fully current; Whitney to verify

- Graham to send Todd the SNR details; Joseph to copy Matt and Jesus on the note
- Two paths discussed: standalone resolution agreement vs. settlement language embedded in a change order
  - Todd previously agreed a change order with finality language is a valid approach
  - Joseph to confirm preferred path with Todd and obtain appropriate language

- Mardale (hand dryers): $1,225 payment tied to hand dryer decision; code-required issue, city not budging; Graham urged to stop delaying and resolve
- Minor: scope complete, no punch list; Chris recommends paying in full; one small \~$5K change order to process
- O\&R: pay $75K, then bring to table and close out; also pricing concrete for new storage (not yet in CRB)
- RightWay: lift station materials on site but ownership unlikely to approve payment; Joseph to advance settlement discussions so RightWay finishes work and transfers materials
- Samtel: needed for \~20 open permits and walk-in cooler warranty; coolers currently jerry-rigged; Samtel called fire marshal, who will not inspect without contractor present; “whistleblower risk” flagged
- Sprinklermatic: needed for storage system tie-in and game-day contingency; same whistleblower/fire chief risk noted
- Steiner Atlantic: threatening repossession of laundry equipment; legal requested update by COB Friday (18th September); Graham to send note to Jose copying relevant parties

# Promethean Payment Reconciliation

- Payments to Promethean (team store + drywall supplementation) need reconciliation
- Chris believes more has been paid than Brian Medina’s log reflects; paid through pay app 5 on stadium drywall and pay app 4 on stadium
- Chris to forward latest figures; full reconciliation to be ready for Monday review

- **Echo $235K Alpha Insulation deduct into the potentially recoverable column**

  Item confirmed as unstarted work; currently left blank pending Graham's direction on recoverability.

  One further reduction not yet forwarded; verify all invoices are current before next payment recommendation.

  Needs Jose's green light before sending; option 1 is steeper discount with payment by end of next week, option 2 is smaller discount paid in two periods.

  Request resolution agreement or change order language with finality clause; target payment teed up for Monday or Tuesday 21st/22nd September.

notes.title: Zoom - Model Fly Thru w/ P+W for Phase 1 + 2
notes.summary_markdown:
# Arena Model Fly-Through: Phase 1 Observations

- Overall reaction positive: “looks like what we were hoping it would”
- Model currently gray/white only; full rendering to come as design advances
- Fly-throughs planned at 50% SD, 100% SD, DD, and CD milestones
- Truss not yet modeled: bottom chord will visually lower the ceiling height
  - Halo board hangs off truss bottom, lowering perceived height further
  - Top white band will go dark once truss is added
- VR walkthrough possible via Revit Enscape with a viewing license

# Concourse Level Layout

- Open concourse on each side: grab-and-go + bar in the middle, restrooms behind solid walls
- Bar on north end faces the stage directly, useful for concerts and sports
- Grab-and-go includes built-in full-height refrigerators, pass-through from service, hot food
  - Half wall preferred over full-height to prevent walk-offs
  - Views out to plaza and Phase 2 from grab-and-go windows
- Concerts: movable curtains close off concourse from bowl along back wall
- Sports: open concourse drives food and beverage sales (“people won’t leave if they feel cut off”)
- Food carts to supplement fixed F\&B (margarita, ice cream, specialty items)
- “Everyman’s club”: 88 seats open to center ice/turf on one side; enclosed club on the other serving two center seating sections
- AV/video control room flagged as needing more space (noted by Santana previous day)
  - Option: split control room and press box to opposite sides

# Suite Level Layout

- Three zone types: loge/loft suites (south arc, open half-walls), club seats (north end, 3 rows), enclosed suites
- All zones share same seating section: bar-height row at suite level, two stepped-down rows in front
- Suite pantries near service elevator; food cooked downstairs and brought up
- ADA: adjustable 42-inch rail on third row, lowers for wheelchair and companion
  - No seats in front of ADA platform; meets over-the-shoulder rule
- No orphan/single seats confirmed; two paired seats under review for sightlines
- Corner suite (angle transition) to be enlarged for AV/video needs
- Island bar or round bar concept floated for suite level center; team to explore bar + grab-and-go configuration
- Announcer/media platform on south arc: potential use for live MESL coverage with turf and halo board as backdrop
- Group seating strategy TBD: club seats or concourse zone; recommend deciding where to locate group sales area

# Seating Dimensions and Halo Study

- Row depth: 34 inches (lower bowl), 36 inches (suites), 33 inches (upper terrace, steep rake requires it)
  - Upper terrace uses 2-foot risers; shallower depth offset by lower seat in front
- Seat width: 20-inch minimum; 21.5–22 inches at suite level and center club
- Halo board study planned: will model size, height, and visibility from concourse, end, suite, and upper terrace levels
  - Goal: align team on correct halo scale for the building before finalizing
- Future expansion (15–20 year horizon): adding an upper level is possible but sightline and stair sizing would need to be addressed now if intended

# Next Steps

- **Share reference photos for club seats, loges, suites, and open concourse clubs** (Don)

  Examples from Henderson and Athens to help the KozPure team visualize each zone.
- **Run full halo board study in the 3D model**

  Show halo size and visibility from concourse, end, suite, and upper terrace levels to align on final scale.
- **Add truss to the Enscape model**

  Once structural consultant completes truss design; will correct perceived ceiling height and halo position.
- **Evaluate AV/video control room enlargement and potential press split**

  Santana flagged need for more space; explore splitting control and press to opposite sides of north end.
- **Decide on group seating zone location**

  Determine whether group sales anchor in club seats (suite level) or a dedicated concourse zone.

---

Chat with meeting transcript: [https://notes.granola.ai/t/9605affe-3122-4eca-9920-8133956519b7](https://notes.granola.ai/t/9605affe-3122-4eca-9920-8133956519b7)
