notes.title: DOVA: Design Team Kick-Off [HOLD]
notes.summary_markdown:
# Project Status and Procurement

- Delivery method changed from design-build to CM at Risk
  - Contracted directly with DOVA LLC (entity for KozPure)
  - Interim letters of agreement going out to all consultants
  - Full contracts to follow during SDs
- CM candidates: Hunt, Turner, Level 10, Suffolk
  - All offering free pre-con support and pricing feedback
  - Formal CM engagement expected after 100% SD package issued
- Target hard cost budget: $225M
  - Down from $300M+ at last engagement in May
  - Key VE items removed: ceiling LED, full exterior LED wrap, modular storage building, Founders Club, speakeasy, 1,500-seat expansion
- Building entity: 194,110 SF (fixed for CEQA exemption, including elevator shafts)

# Schedule Overview

- SD start: 9/14; 50% SD: \~10/16; 100% SD: \~11/20
- Planning Commission hearing: 9/30
- City Council meetings: 10/26 and 11/2 (land transfer, revenue agreements)
- DD start: 11/23 (with possible 2-3 week pause for CM pricing feedback before advancing)
- 50% DD / underground utility permit set: \~New Year’s
- Superstructure permit package: 3/25/27
- 50% CDs and final CDs: mid-June 2027
- Groundbreaking target: 1st January 2027 (18-month build to \~7th July 2028 substantial completion)
- No hard-and-fast opening event committed yet; July 2028 is a target

# Key Open Decisions

- Concrete vs. steel at ground/concourse level
  - Strong lean toward concrete for lower levels (schedule, fireproofing, cost)
  - Hunt also pushed for concrete or hybrid
  - Proceed with concrete assumption; Whitney to informally poll CM candidates for feedback
  - China steel option also to be investigated
- Precast treads/risers vs. SPS system for bowl seating
  - SPS was McCarthy’s recommendation due to local precast availability concerns
  - Primary local precaster (Golden 1, Levi’s) now focused on data centers, pricing up
  - Team preference is precast; early decision needed
  - Upper bowl cantilevers may favor SPS (lighter); study both options by 50% SD
- HVAC strategy: minimum 4 air handlers on roof confirmed; 2 is not feasible
  - Roof plan needed to determine flattening of inner oval to fit units
  - Preliminary AH locations from ME Engineers requested within one week of receiving roof plan
- Halo/center-hung scoreboard size
  - Ceiling LED board: removed; exterior full-wrap LED: removed
  - Halo retained; size TBD via separate design study (sightline views from all 3 levels)
  - i5LED (Rancho Cordova) is the LED vendor; power spec and weight info already circulated
  - Halo preliminary weight: \~125,000 lbs per WJHW calc; i5 range: 350K-550K lbs
  - Exterior front LED: high-res solid panel (no mesh); controller needs to be within \~10 ft of board
- NVAC decision needed
- End-back (loading dock back room) location
  - 95% likelihood it moves off-site (Phase 2/3 movie theater area)
  - If removed, significant loading dock and storage space recovered
  - Decision needed within \~2 weeks
- Sky/rigging grid: Josh texted requesting “sky grid ready, concave not flat”
  - Clarification pending; likely means walkable rigging grid
  - Fall protection tracing ring beams may substitute; cost \~$2M
- Potential WNBA tenancy (under NDA)
  - Would substantially increase broadcast, camera, and lighting requirements
  - Likely triggers NBA lighting levels; cost implication flagged
  - Confirm requirements or explicitly rule out the scenario before finalizing broadcast, camera, lighting, and locker-room planning

# Civil and Site Improvement Plan

- Cannot pull foundation permit until site improvement plan is approved
- Rough grading permit approved ahead of SIP; all other permits gated on SIP approval
- SAC Sewer not part of expedited city agreement; needs separate coordination
- Key information needed from design team:
  - Water/sewer points of connection and fixture unit flows (preliminary in 2 weeks; locked by week 6 / \~50% SD)
  - Fire pump room location (target: next week)
  - Roof drainage locations and pipe sizes (4-6 connections around perimeter; within \~1 month)
  - Building exterior footprint frozen (target: 2 weeks)
  - Site lighting plan (currently out of scope; needs resolution)
- Offsite improvements required per traffic study; some several miles from site
  - Timing trigger unclear; Phil to research
- Mass grading plans: discuss with heavy civil contractor whether advantageous given January start
  - Charlie provided contractor names (Tykert and others); Phil and Whitney to meet with them week of 9/28
- Landscape plans: COA requires final landscape/irrigation plan prior to building permit issuance (not site permit)
  - Separate civil and landscape submittals likely permissible; confirmation needed
- Site lighting: currently out of scope; city entertainment district zoning has specific requirements
  - Animated signage not permitted per current code reading; DOT sign rules also to be checked
- Water pressure: 30-inch transmission main on west edge; hydrant flow test needed to confirm if fire pump/booster pump can be avoided
- Golden State Water: application submitted; follow-up meeting needed on water loop strategy

# Structural

- Deliverables by 50% SD (10/16):
  - Column grids locked
  - Roof shape confirmed (horizontal and vertical, including end facets for AHU placement)
  - Preliminary structural options: concrete concourse and below; concrete vs. steel above concourse
  - Preliminary footing sizes (bulk of ground-level columns; lateral system TBD after 50%)
  - Precast vs. SPS study for upper bowl
- Superstructure permit package: 3/25/27
- Baseline load criteria needed from all disciplines:
  - Halo/LED: use 500,000 lbs (i5 range 350K-550K; team said use 500K or round up to 1M)
  - Exterior wall LED, AHUs, rigging, hydraulic piping (6-inch+ diameter), solar (nominal; confirm owner preference)
- Solar: California Energy Code requires stating design loads for future solar-readiness; default is not to include but must document
- Ice floor: nothing below the 85x200 slab (no conduit, no utilities); cooling/heating pipes \~18 inches deep

# MEP and Utilities

- SMUD/PG\&E coordination: top priority; Whitney to schedule meeting next week
- JCI contracting direct with owner (not under GC); can order long-lead equipment as soon as sizing is confirmed
  - Generator and switchgear flagged as very long lead; order as early as possible
  - JCI to confirm what is included in CUP scope (chillers, cooling towers, main/emergency electrical, boilers)
- Fire pump/booster pump: may be avoidable if water pressure is sufficient; hydrant test needed
  - If needed, could live in CUP building; routing above grade preferred (avoids seismic issues)
  - Fire control center to co-locate with security room
- Video/AV control room: current room (\~10 ft deep) insufficient for full video production
  - Options: truss-mounted (as in Tulsa) or ground level (space very limited)
  - WNBA scenario would substantially increase broadcast room requirements
  - Spotlights on catwalk will have obstructed sightlines with large halo; needs study
- DAS strategy TBD: single integrated system vs. separate carrier head ends; room sizing dependent
- Smoke control: FP to provide preliminary exhaust airflow estimates \~1 week before 100% SD
- Grease interceptors: AHJ meeting needed; individual units per concession vs. central pit is key question
- Energy model: Title 24 compliance pathway one-pager for SDs; full model to follow; coordination meeting with Maura (Perkins and Will energy team) to be scheduled after 50% SD
- Ice conditions: design to AHL standard (50°F dew point); desiccant units under consideration
- Superheat confirmed for home team locker room (double doors); not required for visitor locker rooms

# Food and Beverage

- F\&B operator RFP in progress; finalized in \~50-60 days
- Main commissary kitchen: 3,400 SF on northwest event level; serves bunker suites and inline club
- Inline club capacity: 280 at 7 SF (effectively 200-250 usable with furniture)
- Key unresolved questions:
  - Cooking in concession stands? (Drives MEP loads, exhaust routing, and commissary sizing)
  - How are clubs used per event type (hockey, MASL, Sac State, cabanas)?
  - In-seat service for cabanas?
  - North club: bar vs. action stations vs. suite support kitchen?
- Dedicated F\&B meeting to be scheduled next week: Perkins and Will, DeRay/Duray, KozPure, Santana
  - Perkins and Will to share past 3,400 SF commissary kitchen drawings as reference
- Santana flagged: Friday marketing meeting with Josh and Charlie on F\&B plan; requested it be pushed to allow coordination first

---

# Action Items by Pull Plan Window

**Week 2: 21st–25th September 2026**

- **Distribute BIM 360 access to all consultants** (Perkins and Will)
- **Issue interim letters of agreement to all consultants** (Levelup-pd)
- **Collect full team rosters and BIM user emails from all firms** (All disciplines)
- **Schedule and hold SMUD and PG\&E coordination meeting** (Whitney / ME Engineers)
- **Schedule F\&B coordination meeting with Perkins and Will, Duray, KozPure, and Santana** (Whitney)
- **Schedule i5LED meeting including ME Engineers, Martin/Martin, and WJHW** (Whitney)
- **Confirm end-back room relocation decision with Josh and Charlie** (Whitney)
- **Get clarification from Josh on “sky grid ready, concave” request** (Whitney)
- **Meet with heavy civil contractors on mass grading and winter start feasibility** (Phil / Whitney)
- **Issue updated architectural floor plans to all consultants** (Perkins and Will)
- **Provide preliminary MEP load estimates and room sizes to civil** (ME Engineers)
- **Confirm fire pump room location on current plans** (ME Engineers / Wood Rogers)
- **Initiate Golden State Water follow-up meeting** (Wood Rogers)
- **Research hydrant flow test process and schedule test** (Wood Rogers)
- **Provide preliminary structural column grid and roof shape to Perkins and Will** (Martin/Martin)
- **Share i5LED power specs and weight documentation with ME Engineers, Martin/Martin, and WJHW** (Perkins and Will)
- **Provide preliminary AHU locations based on roof plan** (ME Engineers)
- **Begin concrete vs. steel study for concourse level and below** (Martin/Martin)

**Week 3: 28th September–2nd October 2026**

- **Hold Planning Commission hearing support** (Perkins and Will / Levelup-pd)
- **Freeze building entry point locations on architectural plans** (Perkins and Will)
- **Confirm exterior building footprint** (Perkins and Will)
- **Hold F\&B coordination meeting: cooking scope and club programming** (Perkins and Will / Duray / KozPure)
- **Hold i5LED technical meeting with ME Engineers, Martin/Martin, and WJHW** (Whitney)
- **Meet with heavy civil contractors on mass grading plan** (Phil / Whitney)
- **Provide revised fixture unit flow estimates if layout has changed** (ME Engineers)
- **Deliver preliminary precast vs. SPS study options for upper bowl** (Martin/Martin)
- **Initiate acoustic approach discussion with WJHW** (Perkins and Will / WJHW)
- **Confirm landscape submittal requirements with City of Rancho Cordova** (Wood Rogers)
- **Research offsite improvement timing triggers from traffic study** (Wood Rogers)

**Week 4: 5th–9th October 2026**

- **Issue updated plans incorporating F\&B and club programming feedback** (Perkins and Will)
- **Hold AV room-by-room programming meeting with KozPure** (Perkins and Will / WJHW)
- **Provide preliminary structural load criteria document** (Martin/Martin)
- **Confirm roof drainage locations (4-6 perimeter connections)** (Perkins and Will / ME Engineers)
- **Deliver preliminary concrete vs. steel options above concourse** (Martin/Martin)
- **Coordinate CUP scope and modular unit layout with JCI** (ME Engineers / JCI)
- **Develop halo design study with sightline views from all three levels** (Perkins and Will / WJHW / i5LED)
- **Confirm DAS strategy: integrated system vs. separate carrier head ends** (ME Engineers / WJHW)

**Week 5 / 50% SD: 12th–16th October 2026**

- **Issue 50% SD package to all disciplines** (Perkins and Will)
- **Lock column grids and roof shape at 50% SD** (Martin/Martin)
- **Make concrete vs. steel decision for all levels at 50% SD** (Levelup-pd / KozPure)
- **Make precast vs. SPS decision for bowl seating at 50% SD** (Levelup-pd / KozPure)
- **Confirm LED scope with Josh and Charlie at 50% SD** (Whitney / Perkins and Will)
- **Conduct accessibility review with Jensen Hughes at 50% SD** (Perkins and Will)
- **Schedule post-50% SD agency pre-meeting (fire, health, building departments)** (Whitney / Perkins and Will)
- **Deliver acoustic approach document for 50% SD incorporation** (WJHW)

**Week 6: 19th–23rd October 2026**

- **Hold agency pre-meeting: fire, health, and building departments** (Perkins and Will / All disciplines)
- **Confirm water and sewer points of connection on civil plans** (Wood Rogers / ME Engineers)
- **Issue updated structural drawings incorporating 50% SD decisions** (Martin/Martin)
- **Provide smoke control preliminary exhaust airflow estimates** (Jensen Hughes / ME Engineers)
- **Advance site improvement plan drawings for city submission** (Wood Rogers)
- **Confirm energy compliance pathway with Maura** (Perkins and Will)

**Week 7: 26th–30th October 2026**

- **Support City Council meeting on 26th October** (Perkins and Will / Levelup-pd)
- **Issue 75% SD coordination drawings to all disciplines** (Perkins and Will)
- **Advance MEP coordination drawings for 100% SD** (ME Engineers)
- **Confirm generator and switchgear sizing for JCI procurement** (ME Engineers / JCI)
- **Submit first civil improvement plan set to city** (Wood Rogers)

**Week 8: 2nd–6th November 2026**

- **Support City Council meeting on 2nd November** (Perkins and Will / Levelup-pd)
- **Issue 100% SD coordination set for internal QC review** (Perkins and Will)
- **Deliver final structural drawings for 100% SD** (Martin/Martin)
- **Deliver final MEP drawings for 100% SD** (ME Engineers)
- **Deliver final civil drawings for 100% SD coordination** (Wood Rogers)

**Week 9: 9th–13th November 2026**

- **Complete internal QC and incorporate all discipline comments into 100% SD set** (Perkins and Will)
- **Confirm CM selection or pre-con partner engagement status** (Levelup-pd / KozPure)
- **Finalize food service operator selection process** (KozPure / Santana)
- **Provide FP smoke control narrative for 100% SD** (Jensen Hughes)

**Week 10 / 100% SD: 16th–20th November 2026**

- **Issue 100% SD package** (Perkins and Will)
- **Issue 100% SD package to City of Rancho Cordova for BPR and fire pre-review** (Perkins and Will / Wood Rogers)
- **Hand off site improvement plan work to Wood Rogers for completion** (Perkins and Will / Wood Rogers)
- **Distribute 100% SD package to CM candidates for GMP-light pricing** (Levelup-pd)
- **Evaluate 2-3 week DD pause after 100% SD for CM pricing review** (Levelup-pd / KozPure)

---

# Ongoing / Untimed Action Items

- **Confirm CM selection or earlier pre-con partner engagement** (Levelup-pd / KozPure)
  - Determine whether a CM or pre-con partner will join before the 100% SD issue.
- **Clarify the NVAC decision** (KozPure / Design Team)
- **Confirm CUP location, footprint, and scope** (ME Engineers / JCI / KozPure)
  - Include whether fire pump and domestic booster equipment can be housed in the CUP.
- **Determine main IT, DAS head-end, and video-control-room strategy** (ME Engineers / WJHW / Perkins and Will)
  - Confirm required space and final location.
- **Confirm WNBA scenario requirements—or explicitly rule it out—before finalizing broadcast, camera, lighting, and locker-room planning** (KozPure / Design Team)
- **Resolve exterior screen wall / loading-dock fence approach** (Perkins and Will / Wood Rogers / KozPure)
  - Confirm height, access door, landscaping, and potential signage or LED treatment.
- **Confirm parking agreements and future-phase utility/site infrastructure decisions** (KozPure)
- **Establish design-team coordination cadence and update the schedule every other week** (Levelup-pd / Perkins and Will)
- **Confirm whether there is a committed opening-date requirement** (KozPure)

notes.title: Zoom - P+W | Level Up | KozPure re: Internal Design Kick-off
notes.summary_markdown:
# Tomorrow’s Consultant Kick-off: Agenda Overview

- Goal: align all consultants on SD marching orders and work backwards to the site development plan (Woodrogers submission)
- Key agenda beats:
  1. Project status walkthrough: what’s in, what’s out, budget, open decisions
  2. Pull plan by discipline: what each consultant needs to succeed in SD
  3. Site civil focus: rough grading, permits, site improvement plan (PG\&E, SMUD, sewer)
  4. MEP coordination: heavy JCI integration, utility direction
  5. Structural direction: concrete vs. steel vs. hybrid (may leverage interested CMs for market input)
  6. Wrap-up: immediate action plans and cadence going forward
- Philip (Woodrogers) doing a call mid-meeting; Sam reserving a breakout room so he can stay
- Duray (food service consultants) attending; Sam adding a dedicated F\&B planning block
- JCI: Brian confirmed remote; Denver-based engineer TBC
- Santana forwarded the invite; Whitney to double-check
- Food service output affects MEP, which affects Woodrogers, which affects site: waterfall dependency flagged

# Cadence and Team Integration

- Owner meetings (Charlie, Josh): every other week
- Collaborative partners to integrate early in design: Santana, JCI, i5LED, Bolden (F\&B operator), low-voltage
- Santana keen to meet Duray to align on concessions program, kitchen flow, and path of travel

# Planning Commission Prep

- Josh tied up with city staff meetings to button up the package ahead of the hearing
- Minor discrepancies being resolved; KozPure has everything from LevelUp’s end
- Slide deck needed for both the 9:30 meeting and the Planning Commission hearing
  - Costner, Perkins \& Will, and Garage all producing slides independently
  - Whitney coordinating to align and compile all decks into one cohesive presentation
  - LevelUp slide to highlight who they are and include the schedule
- 26th October: first City Council meeting

# Event Level: Entries, Clubs, and Cabanas

- Main south entry: vestibule with escalator right and cascading linear stair to concourse
- Premium entries on diagonals: direct access to clubs, bunker suites, floor, and cabanas
  - Added third premium entry on west side (per prior Josh/Charlie feedback on Golden One congestion)
  - Ticket office/concierge at west premium entry; 2x 3-ft doors for bunker suite access
- Cabanas: 2 rows on south end (telescopic seats removed to create headroom)
  - Row 1: slightly elevated above dashers; Row 2: further elevated
  - 8 arena seats added directly behind the net as a new premium product (sellable in groups of 2 or 4)
  - Dual-sided ADA lift for Row 2 cabanas (redundancy in case of breakdown)
- End/Inline Club reconfigured:
  - Center bar added (alcohol-centric, high-volume)
  - F\&B support area with back-loaded refrigerators, hot food pass-through, and dry goods/checkout
  - Mastgen grab-and-go machines referenced: San Jose saw \~175% sales increase and reduced lines
  - F\&B open to public; direct access to floor for concerts (dasher removed at inner curve)
- East Club and North Club:
  - Dotted walls = movable hotel-style partitions (meeting room flexibility)
  - North Club: flex room for press, interviews, meet-and-greet; own F\&B prep off north end
  - Decision pending: pass-through window vs. door into club (buffet/action stations vs. concession)
  - F\&B prep area kept on north to avoid blocking future bunker suite expansion
  - Capacity of inline club: \~200 people at 7 sq ft/person
- Bunker suites: 3 on east, 3 on west (equal); option to add more on west between portal and Suite 12
- Restrooms: shared diagonal corner restrooms for club and bunker suite users (surveys show women prefer this over in-suite toilets)

# Back of House: Locker Rooms and BOH Functions

- Home team locker room (center): designed for hockey (largest team); shared/neutral decor, electronic team customization
  - Street changing room, restroom (4 showers, 4 toilets, dry sauna, cold plunge), 24-player locker room
  - U-shape layout; 3-ft carrels, 4-ft for goalies; TV/whiteboard; equipment/stick storage
  - Players’ lounge, coaches’ locker room, sports medicine, strength and conditioning
  - WNBA feasibility: works for game day activation; would need a separate dedicated training facility
- Visitor locker rooms: 4 total, split 2 north / 2 south to separate competing teams
  - Each pair: vestibule, 3 labs, 2 toilets, 3 showers, unisex (no urinals)
  - Sports medicine accessible from visitor side (lockable from home side)
  - Movable wall option to connect Visitor 1+2 internally (not shown; reduces locker space)
- Star/green rooms (3): all identical with shower, sink, ADA toilet; used for officials, halftime performers, or additional stars
  - Josh suggested renaming all three “star rooms”
- Security room: positioned with window overlooking loading dock and corner portal circulation
- Shop, main IT closet (DAS-capable), ADA restroom, and scissor stair also on event level
- Central utility plant: chillers, cooling towers, boilers, main electrical (per JCI assumption)

# Concourse Level: F\&B, Restrooms, and Amenities

- 4 arrival points: escalator, linear stair, 2 elevators (SW and SE)
- F\&B distribution strategy: neighborhood model to minimize walking
  - South center: bar (concert-facing; \~80% of sales); grab-and-go wings on either side
  - East and west: prep areas + grab-and-go; food carts in designated north-south lanes
  - North: grab-and-go or potential full bar (TBD)
- Restrooms: double-loaded women’s, paired men’s/ADA; doors removed for flow; California ADA requires 6.5-ft depth
- West club: serves 2 center sections; wider seats; food prep and ADA in middle
- Seat count: currently 56 over the 7,500-seat soccer target
- Sensory room (NW) and first aid (NE); Don suggested flipping them (first aid closer to loading)
- Guest services: no dedicated space currently; Whitney flagged the need; Don suggested south side near escalator top

# Suite Level and Upper Concourse

- Suite level: low suites and lofts on south, suites on sides, angled suite on north; large open-to-below void on sides creates tall/airy feel
- AV and press box on north; 3-4 rows of club seats on north (sellable individually or as groups)
- Glass at suite level: removed to allow exterior video board on south face; could add glass on east/west sides in SD
  - See-through video board (like T-Mobile/Vegas) would allow glass + board but costs more per sq ft
- Upper concourse: intentionally tight but designed to feel vibrant
  - Bar in center of each east/west run; grab-and-go north and south of each bar
  - Plate rail on north diagonal sections: standing or bar stool seating for 5 sections
  - North end sold as group party zone (NW and NE separately, or full north)
  - Restrooms: east, west, south; ADA on ends facing stage; very few seats on north so no restrooms there
- Halo board: current drawing shows smaller version; sightline studies to be done from multiple seating locations in SD
  - Larger version (red outline) roughly proportional to 85x200 rink/turf

# Design Review Process and Next Steps

- Plans shared with Charlie and Josh today for review; consultants see them tomorrow
- Don advocated for one more internal design review before Dova Phase 2 submission; Josh agreed
  - Rationale: get gut-check on tower shape and massing before locking in
  - Don to assess drawing progress after tomorrow’s internal meeting and schedule accordingly
- Sam to send updated floor plans to Whitney, Charlie, and Josh

# Next Steps

- **Confirm JCI Denver engineer attendance for tomorrow**

  Brian confirmed remote; local engineer TBC. Whitney spoke to him yesterday.
- **Verify Santana received tomorrow's meeting invite** (Whitney)

  Whitney to resend if needed.
- **Distribute high-level agenda to Charlie and Josh** (Whitney)

  So they can decide when to dial in remotely tomorrow.
- **Coordinate Planning Commission slide deck compilation** (Whitney)

  Align Costner, Perkins \& Will, Garage, and LevelUp slides into one cohesive deck for both the 9:30 meeting and the hearing.
- **Send updated floor plans to Whitney, Charlie, and Josh** (Sam)

  For review before and after tomorrow's consultant meeting.
- **Schedule Dova Phase 2 design review with Charlie and Josh** (Don)

  One additional review before submission; Don to assess drawing status after tomorrow's internal meeting.

---

notes.summary_markdown:
# Graham Email: Outstanding Items List

- Whitney sent Graham a compiled list of outstanding items this morning (\~10am)
  - Pulled from Thomas’s action items and Joseph’s prior email
  - Framed around the original unanswered email as the biggest unresolved item
  - Organized chronologically: 9/3 items, then 9/7 (Joseph’s email, copied verbatim)
- Joseph approved sending as-is: “more is more” in this case
  - Referenced Mark Twain: “If I had more time, I would’ve written a shorter letter”
- Email sent live during the call, in advance of the José Mas meeting this afternoon

# Change Order Log: Column Split Proposal

- Joseph proposed splitting the change order column into two:
  - Contractor change order requests
  - Owner (CRB) change order requests
- Rationale: separates true risk from unverified deducts
  - The $2.7M deduct hasn’t been presented to or agreed by the contractor, so shouldn’t be netted in
  - Result still ties to the same total (e.g. 630 + (-4) = 626), but with clearer story
- Whitney’s preference: show positive vs. negative, since negatives are unverified
  - Exception: OSIP items, which are verified
- Graham’s concern: splitting columns could appear to change the 622/626 number
  - Joseph’s view: same number, just more nuanced; cleaner for litigation scenarios

# Customs Credit Reconciliation

- Net credit against S\&I from customs: $747,718 (Graham’s calculation)
- Needs to be added manually as a line item in the full-stack tracker
- Joseph will note the amount in chat for reference

# Procore Access and Data Download

- Full Procore access now secured
- Joseph flagged that relevant data hasn’t been downloaded yet, given bandwidth constraints
- Wants to schedule a session with Whitney and junior Ankura staff
  - Goal: identify and extract closeout-relevant information
  - Deploy junior team onto the download/purge mission

# Next Steps

- **Split change order log into two columns and add customs credit line** (Whitney)

  Separate contractor vs. owner CORs; add $747,718 customs net credit as a reconciliation line in the full-stack tracker.
- **Coordinate with Lemartec on column split**

  Column restructure requires Lemartec's involvement to implement correctly.
- **Request the Ankura presentation from Graham** (Whitney)

  Joseph sent it to Graham only; ask Graham to forward it so Whitney can provide comments.

  Identify and extract closeout-relevant information now that full access is secured.

notes.title: Zoom - Dova Project re: COA review
notes.summary_markdown:
# Planning Commission Scope

- Planning Commission acts as recommending body only; City Council takes final action
  - DA and RPA require City Council action, so full package goes to Council
- RPA should not go to Planning Commission at all
  - Charlie to call Arlene to confirm notice and what’s actually being brought forward
  - Notice published in paper Friday; public notice date is 18th September
- Items confirmed for Planning Commission: CEQA exemption, design review, land transfer agreement
- DA and RPA do not technically need Planning Commission action

# COA Review: Master Conditions

- COA 10: CUP (Central Utility Plant) does not need to be expressly added
  - Covered by “associated improvements” language and incorporated by reference to project plans
- COA 13 (noise/3 AM): deferred; requires separate zoning code amendment via ordinance
- COAs 31, 32, 82: flagged for removal
  - Added by Kim; conflict with current RPA direction (prevailing wage, not public bidding)
  - Creating textual inconsistency: RPA adopted simultaneously with COAs would conflict
  - All three should be pulled until RPA is finalized
- COA 22 (Sac Metro condition): flagged; working to remove and fold into DA instead
  - Sac Metro attorney (Stephen Fire) agreed; city to cover cost under DA
  - SoFi lawsuit precedent: economic components should not go into DA; David to receive email on this
- COA 87: to be removed from COAs; addressed within the suite of project agreements (DA or RPA)
  - David and Matt aligned: conditions should not require going back to hearing bodies for amendments
  - Language should live in agreements, not COAs

# Police Department Parking (COA 20)

- COA revised to 21 visitor spaces, non-designated, within walking distance of police station
  - Previously carved out from arena property and designated police-only; pushed back successfully
  - Spaces can be in temporary lots, replacement parking, or permanent facilities
- Mercury Solis lot (100+ spaces across street) could accommodate the 21 spaces
- Spaces required all the time, not event-day only
- Matt flagged: 6 new onsite stalls already added via police driveway reconfiguration
  - In effect, project is providing 27 spaces total if 21 additional are required
- Dispute over whether current Kilgore Street parking is legal (bike lane); city staff parks there informally
- Strategy options:
  - Consent and let Planning Commission or City Council question the 21-space requirement
  - Flag non-consent, risking loss of hearing date
- Charlie and Josh to meet with police department directly to negotiate down from 21 spaces

# Caltrans Condition: Sunrise Interchange

- Caltrans now requiring analysis of full Sunrise interchange, not just Zinfandel eastbound off-ramp
  - Significant expansion: Matt estimates tripling to quadrupling of effort and cost
  - Requires new traffic counts; existing data used for Zinfandel not sufficient
- Risk flagged: Sunrise is largely built out; any required widening or right-of-way acquisition would be multi-year, multi-million dollar
- Project is not legally required to comply; Caltrans has no jurisdiction, but Albert does not want to challenge them
- Two paths identified by David:
  1. Renegotiate: city retains approval authority over analysis results; Caltrans only signs off on final improvements (Sunrise stays in)
  2. Hold condition as-is but remove Sunrise entirely; deliver Zinfandel analysis only
- Risk of renegotiating: any attempt to revise the condition could cause Caltrans to withdraw it entirely, resetting the process
- CalSTA outreach floated as indirect lever, as it worked previously to advance the condition

# Caltrans Condition: Trigger Date

- Current trigger: prior to first inspection of rough concrete/MEP; flagged as problematic by Matt and Whitney
  - Caltrans interprets this as requiring approved improvement plans, not just submission
  - Approved plans could take 6-12+ months after analysis completion
- Josh spoke to Albert during the call:
  - Albert cannot move trigger to TCO; Caltrans would not accept (they would be blamed for delays)
  - Albert will double the timeline and propose a revised trigger point; to advise tomorrow
- Preferred language (Whitney’s draft, circulated during call):
  - Change “approved by” to “submitted for approval by” first inspection
  - Add 90-day extension clause: if Caltrans review exceeds 90 days, deadline extends day-for-day
  - Final permit obligation tied to TCO or substantial completion for the arena
- Matt: right-of-way acquisition burden must fall on the city, not the developer
  - Precedent already set in other COAs (city takes lead on ROW acquisition)
  - If ROW cannot be obtained, project moves forward; city steps in or waives condition

# CEQA Handling of Sunrise

- Sunrise will not be referenced in the CEQA document
  - Under SB 743, level-of-service improvements are not a CEQA metric; VMT is the standard
  - Any future improvements would be speculative and therefore excluded
- Global statement to be added: any subsequent improvements subject to all applicable laws, including CEQA review
- Blue language (Palmer’s suggested addition) will not be shared with Caltrans
  - City will address CEQA concerns in a separate condition Caltrans does not see or sign off on

# Public Works Conditions

- COA 29: significant risk flagged by Matt
  - If parking location changes substantially from approved LTA, full reanalysis of offsite intersections required
  - Could add or remove required improvements; Sunrise impact unknown until parking is finalized
  - Matt to send Charlie/Josh a map marking acceptable and unacceptable parking zones
- COA 38/39 (Trade Center Drive and Sunrise): right-of-way acquisition for stacker truck access
  - City agreed to take lead on ROW acquisition; developer pays fair share of improvement costs
  - Cost included in Matt’s ROM estimate; language to be added to COA 39 confirming fair-share basis
- COA 35/36: signal modifications and phased access plan updates; no major objections
  - Plan will evolve as subsequent project phases come online; David and Matt aligned this is reasonable
- Table XX: 27 offsite improvement items combining city, SACRT, and SACDOT conditions; Philip sent updated version Monday

# Next Steps

- **Call Arlene to obtain published notice and confirm Planning Commission agenda items** (Charlie)

  Notice went to paper Friday; published 18th September. Confirms definitively what's being brought forward.
- **Send David email on SoFi DA lawsuit** (Charlie)

  Recent ruling relevant to keeping economic components out of the DA.
- **Meet with police department to negotiate parking spaces below 21** (Charlie, Josh)

  Also confirm spaces apply only while police station remains at current location; update COA 20 language accordingly.
- **Request Albert add "to the satisfaction of the Public Works Director" language to Caltrans condition** (Charlie/Josh)

  Albert to advise on revised trigger point by tomorrow; target TCO or substantial completion language.
- **Circulate Whitney's proposed Caltrans condition redline to the group** (Whitney)

  Includes submission-vs-approval language change, 90-day Caltrans review extension clause, and TCO permit trigger.
- **Send parking zone map to Charlie and Josh** (Matt)

  Mark acceptable and unacceptable parking locations to frame the COA 29 reanalysis risk.
- **Add fair-share cost language to COA 39**

  Confirms developer pays fair share, not full cost, of public works improvements.
- **Remove COAs 31, 32, 82, and 87 from conditions package** (Charlie)

  Confirm with Arlene; these will be addressed within the DA and RPA instead.

---

Chat with meeting transcript: [https://notes.granola.ai/t/2a57c8b4-da2f-4908-aada-e5286ddd642b](https://notes.granola.ai/t/2a57c8b4-da2f-4908-aada-e5286ddd642b)

# Infrasub System (Audio)

- New direction: infrasub (low-frequency extension) to be added to audio system
  - Described as an array of \~32 giant subwoofers, each roughly refrigerator-sized
  - Believed to be in HoloPlot’s Concept Plus presentation; not confirmed in Vanguardia model
  - Not yet a commercial product, still in development
- Tom/Brennan to add to radar and get more detail from Derek

# Drum Roof and Floor Level Options

- Three options reviewed to avoid fireproofing the drum roof:
  1. Raise structure only (more space, increases volume slightly)
  2. Split-the-difference hybrid: raise roof \~4 ft, lower staff/donut level \~3 ft
  3. Lower mechanical floor more aggressively (rejected: encroaches on IMS access)
- Leading option is the hybrid (option 2)
  - Level 5 drops from \~20 ft floor-to-floor to \~17 ft
  - Large inflated duct behind IMS would need to shift; may split into two or work with fabric duct vendor on shape
  - Level 6 (donut level) actually benefits mechanically: larger systems run overhead there

# MER Access Floor and Slab Drop

- MER slab drop assumed at \~24 inches total

notes.title: NHS6 - Weekly Enclosure Coordination
notes.summary_markdown:
# Introductions: New Sphere Team Members

- Jeff Hamman leading the Sphere Maryland project
- Rebeca Golden on design side
- Larry Golden, VP of Construction Onsite (joining calls this week, catching up)
- Joe LaPara, project manager from D\&C, joining from studios and the original Las Vegas Sphere build
  - Extensive background in LED interior and exterior systems
- Katie Abek, project manager (not on call), will be on site
- Guido Perego, project manager for technology division, working with Tom and Darren
  - Served as owner representative for audio on the Las Vegas project

# Exterior Enclosure Systems: Evaluation Matrix

- Buro Happold tasked with broad evaluation of exterior systems against Sphere Maryland wish list
  - Key criteria: dark/matte finish, acoustic performance, modularity
- Three systems under evaluation: insulated precast concrete, cold-formed metal frame panel, unitized curtain wall mega-panel
- Matrix document in progress: Excel tracker categorizing systems across multiple criteria buckets
  - Criteria include acoustics, cost, maintenance, and other factors
  - Next step: circulate this week for team to rank criteria by importance to the project
- Sphere team asked to use RAG (red/amber/green) and good/better/best ranking format
- Acoustic layer (Buro Happold) to be tied into the matrix alongside thermal/environmental criteria
- Concept Plus acoustic report assumed a 6-inch concrete shell as baseline for acoustic performance
  - Manica architectural report envisioned precast panel with rail carrier and Sentry panel

# Precast Concrete System

- Key advantage: finish achievable on both interior and exterior faces; insulation contained within panel
- Weight remains the heaviest option of the three systems
- Jointing: two lines of sealant at both vertical and horizontal joints (belt and suspenders)
  - Cracking on exterior surface does not necessarily telegraph through the full panel
- Pushback noted on crack control; preference expressed for rain screen as belt-and-suspenders approach
- Local suppliers within roughly a 4-hour drive; numerous precast suppliers in Canada with US project history
- Next step: quick conversation with structural (Sarah Root) to confirm loads held for exterior wall assembly

# Cold-Formed Metal Frame Panel and Unitized Curtain Wall Systems

- Cold-formed metal frame: joint condition identified as the main area for further evaluation
  - Relies solely on sealant joint (two lines); no gasketed system
  - Multiple contractors in region capable of building to finish; various finish options (metal panel, stucco, etc.)
- Unitized curtain wall mega-panel: gasketed male/female connection at both vertical and horizontal joints
  - Does not rely solely on sealant; weather sealant applied inboard without a second-pass requirement
  - Likely the most expensive of the three systems
- Two manufacturers flagged for curtain wall approach: Eastern (Pennsylvania) and Island Exteriors (Long Island, NY)
  - Buro Happold can arrange presentations with either if Sphere team wishes
- Clover system recap: metal panel on steel frame, sealant joint only, no drainage cavity
  - Closer to a surface barrier system than a true rain screen
  - Capacity to add a second metal layer exists but adds depth and cost

# Roof Waterproofing Strategy

- Dome surface: spray polyurea proposed as primary robust waterproofing layer
  - Spray foam above polyurea, then finished surface
  - Rationale: Vegas spray foam system deemed insufficient for higher-demand Maryland conditions
- Flat/conventional roof areas: cover board system with membrane (spray or cold fluid applied) plus walk pads
  - Hot fluid applied not recommended due to slump risk and application complexity
- Transition between dome and flat: seamless if polyurethane fluid-applied system used throughout
- Products under consideration: Guardian and Henry ProDeck
- Reflectance requirements under IPC energy code must be addressed while avoiding bright white finish
- More rooftop equipment and access expected vs. Las Vegas; long-term durability a priority

# Below-Grade Waterproofing

- Groundwater table is shallow: 4 to 6 feet below grade
- Proposed robust system: blind-side waterproofing below slab, post-applied to walls
  - Components: insulation, membrane, reverse asphalt, drainage mat
  - Products considered: Tremco Supreme 1000, Oximate, Grace 3000
  - Perimeter drain and sub-slab drains (approx. every 5 feet) per geotech recommendation
- Current assumption: full slab waterproofed, not just pits and trench
  - Team to revisit whether full-slab extent is warranted vs. a simpler system in lower-risk zones
- Geotech environmental testing (soil contaminants) still in progress
- Terrazzo floor finish flagged as a risk: any water migration could cause failure
  - Breathable or tile alternatives discussed as potentially more forgiving
- Next step: Buro Happold to produce slab edge plan with one-line diagram showing 4D trench location and good/better/best waterproofing assembly recommendations by zone

# Steel Coating and Additional Enclosure Topics

- Structural steel coating (large steel cage wrapping the building) needs to be incorporated into the enclosure strategy
  - Intumescent coating previously discussed; team to confirm whether it remains the right system for a non-coastal, high-humidity Maryland climate
  - Cost-conscious approach: confirm whether intumescent is the minimum acceptable or the preferred system
- Blast/threat mitigation: Jensen Hughes engaged; their findings may eliminate certain facade systems
  - Proximity threats (vehicles, backpacks) being evaluated; report pending
- RWBI wind loading analysis underway; snow and ice loading to be addressed in a later phase
- FM Global insurance requirements: not confirmed as applicable at this time
  - Team curious about cost delta if FM Global standards were applied to roof and waterproofing design
  - Intent is to be master label prepared and designed to standard, but not necessarily execute the label

# Next Steps

- **Circulate exterior systems comparison matrix to Sphere team** (Buro Happold)

  Send this week for criteria ranking; include RAG and good/better/best scoring; tie in acoustic performance data.
- **Produce slab edge plan with waterproofing assembly diagram** (Buro Happold)

  Show 4D trench location and good/better/best assembly options by zone to right-size the below-grade system.
- **Confirm structural loads held for exterior wall assembly**

  Coordinate with Sarah Root to verify what loads are assumed for the exterior wall, given precast weight implications.
- **Send preliminary enclosure presentation to TVS for distribution to Sphere team** (Buro Happold)

  TVS to distribute; also upload to ACC separately and attach to meeting minutes.
- **Loop steel coating strategy into overall enclosure presentation**

  Confirm whether intumescent is the right system for Maryland's climate and where it sits on the good/better/best scale.

---

notes.summary_markdown:
# SD Kickoff Kickoff

- SDs formally commencing with Perkins Will, as of end of last week
- Kickoff meeting scheduled for Thursday (this week), 9:30 AM to 4 PM in Denver
  - Internal Cosper team meeting the day before, no design consultants
  - Full kickoff includes all design consultants
  - Brian to attend in person; Mike remote (in LA)
  - JCI’s Colorado-based engineer (Vince) may join in person if available
- Agenda being finalized with Sam; will be sent to Brian by end of day Tuesday
  - Brian has a 9-10 AM conflict (CSULA appointment); that slot is just intros/objectives
- SDs run through mid-November to 100% SD phase
  - Whitney to schedule coordination meetings with JCI, utility providers, and other partners throughout

# Estimate Walkthrough

- JCI scope broken into 5 buckets, each with distinct pricing structure:
  1. JCI-manufactured equipment (air handlers): 12% OH + 10% profit margin; material only to GC
  2. Non-JCI equipment (interior lighting fixtures): OH markup only, no profit; material only to GC
    - Exhaust fans excluded: JCI doesn’t manufacture them; better procured directly by GC
  3. Turnkey pass-throughs (Simco ice equipment, i5 Lighting): OH markup only
    - Ceiling LED scope removed (cost); halo and partial exterior board still in
    - i5 estimate includes ceiling LED; Brian to annotate what’s actually in scope
  4. BMS/controls: carried as a budget, no markup; controls team goes direct to GC for arena
    - $3.5M figure; $600K for cup installer moved back to separate bucket
  5. Switchgear/electrical: standard OH\&P markup, but highly uncertain (+/- 50-100%)
    - Installation likely better contracted to GC’s electrical sub to reduce complexity
- Central utility plant: JCI acting as turnkey DBGC with standard OH\&P; connections to 5 feet from building
- Financing and construction treated as separate negotiations; OH\&P not cross-pollinated with financing interest

# Indirects and GCs

- Bonds: straightforward, broken out separately
- Deal development fee: covers pre-design work and finance team structuring; aligns with pre-development letter
- JCI scope development: engineering costs through notice to proceed
- Professional services (legal): blank for now; only triggered if lender requirements demand external counsel
- Construction risk/contingency: carried to maintain flexibility on top-line number
  - Won’t be returned to Cosper; reduces financed amount if unused
  - Sensitive to Josh and Charlie’s ongoing equity negotiations with other lender; reducing the $76M financed amount not in anyone’s interest right now
- Transition scope: covers staffing, training, office, tools, and parts for long-term O\&M of central plant (and likely ice equipment)
- GC labor: 6 staff in year 1, 5 in year 2
  - Year 1 includes engineering manager (tapers off as construction engineer ramps)
  - Core team: project executive, project director, 2 site supers, construction engineer, contracts admin
  - Other GC costs (year 1 and 2): temp facilities, utilities, office supplies, travel

# Next Steps

- **Send SD kickoff meeting invite and agenda to Brian and Mike** (Whitney)

  Agenda with Sam to go to Brian by end of day Tuesday so he can plan around his 9-10 AM conflict.
- **Add scope and markup notes to estimate, then send to Whitney** (Brian)

  Annotate material-only vs. install, clarify i5 LED scope (ceiling, halo, exterior boards), and add scope description per bucket.
- **Check Vince's availability for Thursday's Denver kickoff** (Mike)

  Colorado-based engineer could join in person; no promises but worth confirming.

---

- Thursday will also finalize FAT plan day-by-day, accounting for ship dates between AeroLab and Tate

- All components ship to Tate first, then Tate ships final to Las Vegas
- AeroLab targeting \~November 20th for fan assembly shipment to Tate

  - Fan running demo at AeroLab, louver/swivel duct demo at Tate for second unit

  - Fog holes in bottom of nozzle duct to be cut before end of week

- 2 Orca fog machines: estimate in hand, cost being shared; dates to be aligned to updated schedule

  - All controls programming, PLC parameter dialing, and 4D effects trials in this block
  - If fan ready early, use actual fan; otherwise test louver cabinet in front of existing shop fan

### Generator, No-Fly Zone \& Access

- Generator quote: original $27K jumped to \~$50K with revised dates (30th to 11th vs. 1st to 8th)
  - Paul to forward AeroLab’s quote (from Javier) for comparison; Sphere to review
  - Feeder cable lengths to be field-verified; currently estimated at \~200 ft (four 50-ft sections per run)
  - AeroLab offered to have their engineer validate the technical proposal if Sphere shares redacted version
- No-fly zone: needs update for 2-foot trench shift for both S6 and S18
  - Paul to get updated drawings to his team; ready for next discussion
  - Stage heights up to 8–10 ft from floor (deck + drum riser) to be factored in
- Las Vegas site access:
  - Parking: Lot M by guard shack; tools via loading dock or carry-in
  - License plate info required for new gate system; AeroLab to provide closer to date
  - Storage options: venue can accommodate work boxes/cases in advance; kitchen as overflow

### Next Steps

- **Build and distribute integrated schedule** (Whitney)

  Send to Victoria and Chris for review before Thursday's call.

- **Finalize FAT plan and distribute** (Paul)

  Go through day-by-day on Thursday call; package and send to all after.

- **Coordinate upright attachment locations with Chris** (Paul)

  Set up Zoom this week with CAD model to confirm upright and swivel duct clearances.

- **Prepare nozzle connection point drawing** (Paul)

  Show tapped hole locations for 4D duct inclusions and cut fog holes in nozzle bottom by end of week.

- **Update no-fly zone drawings for S6 and S18** (Paul)

  Reflect 2-foot trench shift; ready for next group discussion.

- **Forward generator quote to Sphere for comparison** (Paul)

  Javier to send; Sphere pulling costs together now.

- **Share contingent worker badge list with Dave** (Victoria)

  Chris's team to also submit names for badge processing.

- **Set up 4D duct attachment meeting**

  Target next week; Friday this week if earlier slot needed.

notes.title: NHS6 - Finalize Holoplot Locations
notes.summary_markdown:
# Background and Design History

- S6 design intent: integrate structural steel, facet layouts, and secondary framing to accommodate Holoplot array locations from the outset
- Shifted from 3x3 to 4x3 row tile facets for larger facets, better array fit, and fabrication economies
- Mohawk stays 3x3 (avoids LED seam down the middle; facet is \~1m narrower than standard)
- Arrays squared up to align with catwalks, but squaring increases 60-degree cone interference with adjacent facets

# 60-Degree No-Fly Zone and Acoustic Occlusions (Workstream 1)

- No-fly zone is 60 degrees for both X1 and X3 series; always been the case
- Two distinct occlusion scenarios identified:
  - Double framing at facet edges colliding with the 60-degree cone
  - Facet framing running directly in front of a Holoplot module
- Current facet perimeter is solid aluminum, not trussed; mockup 2 perimeter was also solid
  - Vegas had trussed perimeters within the cone; S6 does not yet
  - Christian confirmed trussing the perimeter is possible for the main contract but requires full structural calculations (months of work)
  - Connector/T-blocks at facet edges cannot be minimized due to structural constraints (edge distances, screws)
- Known acoustic impact: a 40-foot, 45mm occlusion causes \~6–8 dB drop above 1 kHz
  - Fully solid trusses would block sound entirely outside the cone
- Agreed approach: identify which specific areas need to be trussed open vs. solid, case by case
  - Blanket trussing not acceptable due to cost
  - Optimization driven by Olly/Fundamental’s impact data

# Speaker Depth and Truss Tolerance (Workstream 1 cont.)

- Target speaker setback: 500mm from front surface; 580–600mm discussed as a fallback
- Truss depth cannot be reduced without increasing member thickness (structural constraint)
  - Minimum 35mm gap required for steelwork tolerance
- Moving speaker back increases cone occlusion footprint: gain in one area, lose in another
- Rasti’s recommendation: fix speaker location first, then optimize member sizes around it
  - If members can’t be reduced, move the speaker; this is a local fix with no wider impact

# Primary Steel Coordination at Poles (Workstream 2)

- Three Holoplot arrays at the poles were the main coordination challenge with primary steel
- Severud’s solution: shift primary steel left and right of the array so no primary sits in front of the blue (Holoplot) bounding box
  - Daniel (Severud) confirmed this approach works
  - Secondary framing can remain standard; just needs to be trussed in front of arrays
- Physical clash check: worst-case bounding box (X1 + X3 combined + 9-inch frame) shows a very tight condition at one bottom-left pole location
  - Not yet confirmed as a physical clash vs. acoustic clash; need actual speaker frame dimensions modeled
  - Darren’s position: don’t move framing over a handful of drivers; need data on actual audience impact first
- Agreed: model X1 and X3 as separate toggleable layers (not combined bounding box) so clashes can be assessed individually
  - Olly/Tom to provide 3 separate models: X1, X3, and bounding box

# FX Array Positions

- Outer two FX arrays (1st and 3rd) are inches away from needing node removal
- Agreed resolution: shift 1st FX array left and 3rd FX array right to clear nodes
  - Adrian (Holoplot) confirmed no acoustic performance impact from this shift
  - Middle FX array stays in place
- Nodes to be added at shifted positions so standard trussed facets can be used in front of FX arrays
- Minor change; no need for formal sign-off from Eric/Jonathan, but team will inform them

# Environmental and Main Array Status

- Environmental arrays: frozen
  - Severud can proceed with primary steel design and hanging point planning
- Main array: fixed (special-case solution, analogous to Vegas)
- PDEs (depth extension arrays, lower arrays): under revision
  - Being consolidated (reducing from 5 elements); update expected by end of this week (Friday 18th September)
  - Current steel shown by Severud will not work once Performer doors are incorporated

# Performer Doors

- Design intent: removable facet panel (like a mini proscenium) with a man door inside it
- David (TVS) shared a sketch showing orange removable facets with doors within them
- Spec has been shared with Sealy; detailed design conversation deferred (not a mockup 3 topic)
- To be added to Wednesday’s design call agenda

# Cone Angle Refinement and Beam Parameters

- Rasti requested cones be updated from blanket 60 degrees to actual required beam angles per array
  - Some environmental arrays beam above seating and may only need \~40 degrees
  - Some pole arrays need full 60 on one side, near zero on the other
  - Reducing cone extents will minimize the trussing zone and reduce cost
- Holoplot beam data received; Olly’s team working through overlaying per-array beam parameters into the model
  - Timeline: models updated this week, beam parameters added the following week
- Note: grating lobes and radiation patterns outside the main beam also need consideration, not just the primary cone

# Array Naming and Wednesday Executive Update

- Array naming: should match Las Vegas for content portability across venues
  - Names exist in SketchUp versions but not on DWGs; Olly/Tom to align with Sphere Audio (Adrian) on naming convention
- Wednesday update with Dibble and Paul:
  - Olly and Tom to connect with Whitney tomorrow (Tuesday 15th September) to align on narrative
  - Key message: array positions are now agreed and frozen; work is now optimization of framing (trussed vs. open), not relocation
  - Olly’s report colors (red/amber/green) have improved: reds moved to ambers; report narrative needs updating to reflect this before Wednesday

# Next Steps

- **Issue X1, X3, and bounding box as 3 separate models to Severud** (Olly, Tom)

  Don't wait until Friday; release environmental and shifted FX arrays as soon as ready so Severud can advance primary steel design.
- **Update FX array positions in the model: shift 1st left, 3rd right** (Olly, Tom)

  Adrian confirmed no acoustic impact; Severud to confirm node additions at new positions.
- **Issue updated location model including PDE revisions by Friday 19th September** (Olly, Tom)

  PDEs being consolidated; Severud needs this to finalize steel and catwalk design.
- **Overlay actual beam parameters per array into the model** (Olly, Tom)

  Target: week of 21st September. Will define must-truss vs. nice-to-truss zones and reduce trussing extent.
- **Update Olly's report narrative and color coding before Wednesday** (Olly)

  Reds have moved to ambers; report must reflect that positions are frozen and work is now framing optimization.
- **Connect with Olly and Tom ahead of Wednesday executive update** (Whitney)

  Align on what is being presented to Dibble and Paul; send invite for Tuesday 15th September.
- **Add Performer door detailed design to Wednesday's design call agenda** (David)

  Not a mockup 3 conversation; needs to be scheduled as a detailed design item.
- **Align array naming convention with Sphere Audio** (Olly)

  Names must match Las Vegas for content portability; coordinate with Adrian.

---

- D5, Glenreader change glass spec tempered/laminated ($7,625): ARQ documentation very limited
  - Only CD detail E1/A561 calls out clear glass, no glass type, dimensioned as half-inch (not code compliant)
  - Specs don’t close the gap; Div 8-8000 leaves glass selection to contractor’s PE
  - Div 057000 specifies 3/4-inch laminated for railing glass under Florida Building Code
  - Glenreader priced from Manica DD narrative: uncoordinated ARQ documentation, narrative carried into CD with nothing behind it
  - Tempered laminated already required by code and specs; upgrading to alpha cladding impact assembly with clamps/cutouts; ARQ as root cause

  - Anchorage method for glass guardrail on thin precast wall is a design decision AOR should have resolved before precast buyout
  - ARQ changed method after contract let and folded it into a building department reissue rather than flagging as design change
  - Left spec in conflict with drawing; cost legitimately owed to Metromont
  - Mitigating factor: a competent GC might have flagged the notch/guardrail conflict proactively
- D7, Baker Concrete West stair demolition: steps found too narrow by city due to railing location; steps built to ARQ drawings; owner chose demolition over rebuild; design issue
- D8, right-way plumbing trench/East Club drains: confirmed per RFI 1468; East Club exterior terrace designed flat; ARQ redesigned to introduce slope and drainage; design oversight

# Change Order Review: D10 to D11

- D10, Alpha insulation CMU walls ($235K): driven by ASI-035; documented design change; covers exterior block walls at event/mezzanine levels and interior block walls at event level; some walls possibly missing from G021 series, flagged for review
- D10, Lots Beach chase wall framing/sheeting/insulation ($311K): ARQ cost
  - RFI 1325 is the key document; LamarTech asked why 4/6-inch CMU chases were buildable given tieback detail
  - Chase wall undersized for toilet carriers; CDs never reconciled to carriers
  - Will summarize via Claude for brevity
- D10, Lots Beach spray foam: removed; miscoordination by LamarTech, not ARQ; spray foam interferes with subroof decking installation
- D11, expansion joint ($220K): complex, documentation sparse
  - RFI 1135 is the key reference; LamarTech assumed EJ stopped at Level 1 and did not enter precast bowl
  - PT’s SSK issued 2 days later says otherwise but provides only manufacturer cut sheets
  - ARQ never issued a detail with the step/precast addition; every waterproofing bidder priced as unknown
  - Still needs further investigation: unclear whether Kenny’s sketch defined bowl joints or whether A1 replaced them
- D11, Alpha additional expansion joints ($125K): reclassified as reinstall, not missing detail
  - Joint was built, pulled out, and redone; likely sequencing issue (LED screen above owner’s suite added after joint complete)
- D11, Alpha insulation monumental stairs ($125K): likely ARQ cost
  - Building expansion joints run down west side stairs 12 and 17 but no fire-rated joint detail following treads/risers in drawings
  - Caveat: space was converted to occupiable use and drawings may not have been updated accordingly

# Next Steps

- **Send updated CO log to Devin** (Whitney)

  Share today's compiled findings on defect tagging and ARQ vs. contractor attribution.
- **Confirm RFI 1135 ownership with LamarTech**

  Clarify why GeForce is listed as responsible contractor and when A1 replaced them; confirm whether any sketch defined the bowl joints.
- **Confirm LED screen ownership with LamarTech (Javier Turbay)**

  Determine whether the LED screen above the owner's suite was an owner add after the expansion joint was complete.
- **Add George's notes for Baker Concrete DO45 (West Field Suites trench drains)**

  George to send updated log; Whitney to pull from old version and incorporate into D2.
- **Await new pricing from Mr. Glass and Burke's Welding**

  New pricing based on George's updated sketch 260904 will supersede current D5 figures; slope rail detail with Rodrigo still pending.

notes.title: Project closeout — punch list valuation, fee reconciliation, and recovery estimates
notes.summary_markdown:
# TSI Punch List and Retainage Assessment

- Retainage standard: value the work, multiply by 2x factor, retain that amount, release the rest
  - Example: $1M work, $200K retainage held, retain $400K, release $600K
- TSI is non-standard: retainage may not be sufficient, needs actual testing and certification
- Request: assessors must look under the hood and confirm if retainage covers punch list risk, not give a generic answer
  - TSI flagged as high-risk: unknown scope (e.g., tile removal cascading into full room demo)

# Punch List Items and Cooperation Gaps (Complaint List for Graham)

- Framing: this is the one opportunity to formally flag TSI’s lack of cooperation, so the list must be airtight and fair
  - Whitney to call Chris and ask George for additional items before finalizing
- Items being documented:
  - Evaluation pending punch list work
  - Procore cleanup and reconciliation
  - Financial trackers used to guide closeout are inconsistent with official project financials (Procore)
  - Change order audit review: CO basis not reviewed; no dedicated support provided despite multiple requests
  - Support in assessing fair value of pending CO recovery savings opportunities
    - Examples: overtime disputes, back charges, LTG
    - TSI tendency to restate subcontractor amounts rather than independently assess
  - Access to Procore (noted as lower priority)
- Pending: results of Procore reconciliation still being worked on by TSI

# Closeout Budget and Fee Structure

- Crawl cost distribution: Graham wants a breakdown of Crawl’s fees by subcontractor (Baker, Miller, Hilliard, etc.) to justify partial payment with ROI framing
  - Whitney emailed the Crawl summary from Graham to the other participant
  - Graham’s ask: reorganize to match closeout strategy
- Monthly staffing costs (Amartek proposal: $308K/month, reduced):
  - Keeping: Francisco, Andres, Andrew Murray (50%), one superintendent, Matt Wasawa, Rodrigo
  - Level Up: Whitney and Justin at $45K/month (Jordan Ward removed)
  - Chris is MFP/MindFrame Park staff, not Level Up
- Legal fees (estimated flat at $50K/month each, pending actual invoices):
  - Troutman Sanders: invoices seen for Oct ($47.7K) and Nov ($27K); using \~$35K as estimate
  - Todd / GTHNY: no invoices available
  - Katten: no invoices; estimated at $50K
- Fee on GC GRs: Whitney flagged potential double-dipping on fees; will push back during LaMarTech audit phase
- Burn rate structure: add a column for fees accrued pre-September (engagement started late August) plus ongoing monthly rate from September forward

# Recovery Estimates and Cash Flow Model

- Whitney’s tracker: filtered for “complete disputed” items and added rough recovery estimates (10-20% of CO value)
  - Current tracker shows \~$12.3M total estimated recovery
  - Back charge columns added by Andrew (Amartek): unclear if these are new or already issued in Procore; Whitney waiting for Andrew to call back to confirm no double-counting
- High/low recovery range methodology agreed:
  - Low: back charges + 15% of CO audit value
  - High: sum without adjustment factor
  - High from Lemartec tracker and Whitney’s tracker combined: take the higher of the two highs, Whitney’s low as the low
  - Current range landing around $5M (low) to $7.5M+ (high); will increase as blanks are filled in
- Cash flow model: built with stages (Stage 0/1/2/3); auto-populates from Whitney’s trackers once values are plugged in
  - Participant to send Whitney a copy of the draft model
- Retainage sufficiency by sub: Whitney and participant to go through each sub and assess if retainage held is enough
  - TSI and Jazz flagged as uncertain; most others likely sufficient
  - Whitney’s plan: use AI with downloaded punch list data and unit rates from Procore to generate educated estimates

# Next Steps

- **Finalize cooperation gap list with Chris and George** (Whitney)

  Call Chris and ask George for any additional pushback or disagreement items before submitting to Graham.
- **Fill in remaining blank recovery estimates in tracker** (Whitney)

  Use AI with downloaded punch list and Procore unit rates to generate educated guesses for all incomplete lines; add high/low columns.
- **Clarify Andrew's back charge columns to avoid double-counting** (Whitney)

  Confirm with Andrew whether the S\&T back charge columns are separate from or already included in the 622/626 line items.
- **Send cash flow model draft to Whitney**

  Participant to share the anticipated cash flow model so Whitney can align tracker columns.
- **Send activity log copy to Whitney**

  Participant owes this email; Whitney wants the sheet for reference.
- **Reconvene mid-afternoon around 1:30 PM**

  Continue working through Graham's six items from last night's email.

notes.summary_markdown:
# O\&M Submittal Deficiency (Rodrigo’s Spreadsheet)

- Lamar Tech’s response is insufficient: only touches \~2 subcontractors, reads as a checklist, not a work product
- Response to Lamar Tech should come from Miami Freedom Park as the client, not the consultant team
- Plan: Joseph to annotate their Excel spreadsheet with specific gaps and examples of what’s expected
  - Lamar Tech doesn’t know they’re falling short; they need a roadmap, not just a rejection
  - Include a format example showing the level of detail required per item (e.g., 10 lock models, each with its own O\&M)

# Payment Recommendations and Closeout Path

- Lamar Tech’s Matt Wasala email re: payment and closeout is a CYA; no response warranted until MFP’s plan is in place
  - Graham needs to present a plan to the board before any payments move; ownership won’t release funds without it
  - MFP’s approach is strategic (risk-weighted by trade), vs. Lamar Tech’s bottom-up “pay through a certain month” approach
- Miller contract math doesn’t add up
  - Contract value: $76M, change orders: \~$12M; Lamar Tech claims $12M recovery potential
  - \~$1.89M of those change orders is straight material cost (Musco Lighting), awarded post-contract, not recoverable
  - $12M recovery target is not realistic given the composition of the change orders
- Kroll’s $25M recovery target is under scrutiny
  - $11-12M of that figure assumed to come from Miller, which is now in doubt
  - Kroll is withholding backup documentation, citing non-payment; team has only draft presentations, no actual work product
  - Kroll’s leverage play: holding support docs to force payment on invoices that haven’t been validated yet

# Cash Flow Forecast for Graham

- Need a forecasted cash flow matrix: \~5 entities x \~5 months, building to an S-curve
  - Entities: LevelUp, Ankara, Lamar Tech, Kroll, legal (Troutman, Top Herbst, Katten)
  - Katten (K-A-T-T-E-N): handling lien responses and drafting
  - LevelUp and Kroll projected through at least November, then at a reduced burn rate
  - CR Solutions: lump sum, not monthly; sales tax audit handled in-house
- Whitney to pull legal invoices (Troutman, Top Herbst, Katten) to establish monthly carry rates
- Follow-up call scheduled for this afternoon to work through the GC/GR line items together

# Next Steps

- **Annotate Lamar Tech's Excel with specific O\&M deficiencies and a format example** (Joseph)

  MFP should send the response; Joseph's notes provide the roadmap for what Lamar Tech needs to deliver.
- **Pull legal invoices for Troutman, Top Herbst, and Katten** (Whitney)

  Needed to estimate monthly legal burn for the cash flow forecast matrix.
- **Build cash flow forecast matrix this afternoon** (Whitney)

  5 entities x 5 months; follow-up call scheduled for this afternoon to work through GC/GR line items together.

- Interim agreement executed 9/7; both sides signed this week
- Perkins Will owed $99,090; client prepared to pay but McCarthy dispute is holding it up
  - McCarthy tagged a \~$100K blanket charge for the Nov 4 to May 1 dead period
  - Client (Cospire/Chuck) disputing that charge; reaching out to McCarthy directly
  - Greg trying to reach Tim at McCarthy to resolve
- Separate billing to Cospire outside McCarthy flagged as legally risky; preference is to get paid through McCarthy
- Goal: don’t let the dispute block SD phase progress

- SD start: 9/8, SD complete: 11/16; 50% DD: 12/28, 100% DD: 2/12
- Groundbreaking pushed to early January at best
  - MDR approval: 9/30; two city council meetings; development agreement final approval: 11/2
  - 30-day NTP wait after 11/2 puts earliest start at 12/11, then holidays
- Site improvement plan: submitted \~12/15, targeting approval by mid-January to early March
  - No heavy construction or underground work until plan approved; rough grading can start January
- Opening: July 6 at earliest (18 months from January start); Hunt estimated 19 months
- Client previously expecting March 2028 and September groundbreaking: both off the table, client now appears aware and realistic
- Utilities (SMUD, PGE, sewer) not yet in schedule; Wood Rogers needs early load/drainage/fixture data to size utilities for site plan

# Key Design Decisions and Stakeholder Coordination

- Concrete ground level, steel above: both Hunt and gut instinct point this way; need contractor confirmation
  - McCarthy was cagey on cost comparison; plan to get gut-check from Hunt and Suffolk
  - Hunt preliminary concrete vs. steel schedule analysis to be forwarded to Sam
- Contractor procurement: no CM on board yet; plan to RFP at 100% SDs
  - AE Hunt stood down for now; Suffolk (hired Will Gamba from Hunt) also in consideration
  - Long-lead items (generators, transformers, switchgear) may need early direct purchase and transfer to CM, as done in Miami

- F\&B (Santana): advising on operator RFQ only, not running the venue
  - Risk: selected operator may override Santana’s design input (seen at Fresno State, Levy North)
  - Preferred approach: get operator to sign off on preliminary drawings before committing, with change-order language if they deviate
- i5LED: sole-source concern noted, but if client insists, integrate with ME Engineers early given major electrical load implications (potential California code issue)
- Bolden (DAS/Wi-Fi integrator): being engaged; ME Engineers also on job for DAS design-build
  - Two DAS approaches: shared room with carrier equipment divided, or single unified system
  - Bring Bolden in early alongside ME, same approach as JCI

# Meeting Cadence and Kickoff Plan

- Two-meeting structure agreed:
  1. Design review with Cospire (Josh and Charlie): target next Wednesday 9/16, 2:00–5:00 PM MT; Whitney to confirm with Orlana
    - Perkins Will to share updated plans with DeRay ahead of this for early feedback
  2. Full internal consultant kickoff: target Thursday 9/17 in Denver, starting 9:30 AM (Friday 9/18 as backup)
    - Attendees: Perkins Will, ME Engineers, Wood Rogers (in-person or remote all-day), DeRay, JCI (remote, TBD on scope)
    - Cospire invited remotely but meeting framed as Denver-based to manage travel cost
- Pull-plan format (McCarthy-style sticky notes) explicitly rejected as chaotic; kickoff to be structured differently
- Sam to advise Whitney on which milestones warrant Santana input and i5 joint sessions with ME

  Message Orlana to get on calendar for 2:00–5:00 PM MT; this is the Perkins Will design update session before the broader kickoff.
