notes.title: Project closeout — lien waivers, payment strategy, and contractor settlements
notes.summary_markdown:
### Closeout Legal Framework (Todd)

- Two lien waivers required with every payment:
  - Unconditional waiver covering all prior payments received
  - Conditional waiver covering the current payment being made
- Final payment: conditional waiver is self-executing once payment clears; no final lien waiver will be pursued
- Resolution agreement required for major trades:
  - Resets contract value to agreed settlement amount
  - Confirms full payment and releases all claims
  - Carves out only unknown future claims, personal injury, death, third-party property damage
- Resolution agreement can be structured as a negative-value final change order if contract language supports it
- Closeout checklist items (warranties, O\&Ms, permits, keys) should be listed as conditions precedent to final payment within the resolution agreement
- Existing contract lien waiver templates should be used with minimal modification; only dollar amounts need updating for partial payments
- Commitment and payment date must be communicated to each trade: if a date is given, it must be honored exactly

### Contractor Groupings: A, B, C

- Group A+: ready to close, checklist nearly complete; straightforward phone call or meeting to finalize
  - Estimated \~18 of 20 in this tier will wrap in 2 afternoons
  - Communication: confirm checklist status, set a closing call or meeting
- Group A/B: good faith or interim payment needed; audit work still in progress
- Group C/D: complex, contested, or deficient scope; heated negotiations expected
  - Examples: Miller Electric, Baker Concrete, Hill York, Samtel
- Scheduling cadence: easy trades front-loaded in weeks 1-2; harder trades in weeks 3-4
- CO date risk: order of trades may shift to protect certificate of occupancy; some C-group trades (e.g., Samtel) may be pulled forward

### Samtel

- Base scope complete; no incomplete kitchen or concession work
- Outstanding items: punch list (minimal), city permit closeout, audit
- Kroll audit identified less than $100K in savings to date
- Change orders were reviewed holistically at job end; significant reductions already negotiated with LamarTech previously
- Backcharge gap: potential backcharges to other trades (e.g., Rightway or Quentin Reader for millwork misalignment) may not have been formally issued; Whitney to verify with Andrew/Andres
  - These do not block Samtel closeout but may affect other trade settlements
- SNR payment (\~$1.75M partial, $250K hold for OSIP reconciliation and punch): punch walk completed; awaiting Steve’s team sign-off
  - Todd to review draft partial lien waiver before payment is released
  - Resolution agreement to cover: price reduction, outstanding items, and payment date certain
- Samtel prioritized for early closeout given permit exposure and TCO risk

### Venuur (Drywall)

- Never formally defaulted; supplemented at risk via Bravo/Promethean (\~$1.5M supplementation cost)
- Bulkhead descoped to Latspeach ($300K change order issued); descope of other work not executed via change order by LamarTech
- Venuur contract: $16.5M; \~$2M deductive change order proposed; Venuur rejected it
- Venuur paid through January (\~$14M+); \~$2.5M remaining including retainage
- Venuur position: claims full remaining contract balance; refuses deduct
- Team position: Venuur owes punch (which they’ve refused), Bravo can cover it; no further need for Venuur
- Recommended approach: have the settlement conversation, let them sue if unwilling; counterclaim for supplementation costs
  - Litigation would likely sit for 3 years; Venuur’s position weakens over time
- FBM/FMB sub-tier supplier risk: if Venuur was paid for that subtrade’s work and didn’t pass it through, owner has exposure; check SOVs to confirm payment alignment

### Certificate of Occupancy Risk

- TCO extension: one free extension available; second extension carries significant cost (potentially 6-7 figures)
- 30 open permits flagged (example: Simon’s Deli kitchen equipment); surfaced for the first time in recent meetings
- Any trade with permit closeout obligations goes to top of priority list
- LamarTech directed to provide specificity on all permit closeout requirements per trade

### $600M Budget Strategy and Recovery Plan

- Current discussion range: $622-624M; goal is to present a credible path to $600M
- Presentation format: 2-page PowerPoint overlay on existing deck (John’s framing, aligned by Graham/Whitney)
  - Page 1: total spend to date, remaining balance, how balance gets spent down to $600M
  - Page 2: payment schedule by month (September, October, November tranches)
  - Page 3 (proposed): resources and cost to execute, including Ankura and Kroll fees by phase
- September payment tranche needed: \~$2-6M (exact number TBD); payments drawn from open contractor pool
- Recovery target: $25M total across 3 buckets:
  1. Trade/subcontractor clawbacks (change order reductions, backcharges): \~$15M realistic; $25M is the high
  2. LamarTech fee, GC, and GR recovery: “money is there,” case needs to be built; previously treated as off-limits
  3. Design errors and omissions (canopy, etc.): larger legal action; some may count toward the $25M, some separate
- $2.3M in tariff/duty recovery already actualized; remaining target \~$22.7M
- Kroll costs flagged as high; only 30-40% of their work product received to date; payment plan being structured by packages tied to trade groups (A, B, C)

### LamarTech Staffing Reduction

- Current September GR burn: \~$1.5-1.6M (flagged as excessive; ZDI alone showing $1M, reason unclear)
- Recommended closeout staffing: 1 senior PM, 1 APM/PE, 1 superintendent, minimal project controls (3-4 hrs/week)
- Candidates discussed:
  - Sala: retain for TCO process (embedded with city, knows full documentation requirements)
  - Rodrigo: retain as APM (broad project knowledge)
  - Frankie Paredes: retain as superintendent candidate
  - Jennifer McNamara: sharp on calls but siloed to interior scopes; not on current GR list
- Action: Whitney, Joseph, and Chris to review the 16-person GR list and mark each as remove or keep by end of day
- Argument to LamarTech: 3% fee on $600M+ project; they can provide a few hours/week of knowledge transfer at no additional cost; if they won’t, escalate to Jose
- LamarTech communications gap: direction was given that LamarTech staff should not discuss money with contractors; all payment discussions to route through owner; unclear if this was followed back to March

### Next Steps

- **Draft and circulate SNR partial lien waiver for Todd's review**

  Payment is \~$1.75M partial with $250K hold; Todd needs to confirm it is comprehensive and protective before release.

- **Verify outstanding Samtel backcharge notices for millwork misalignment** (Whitney)

  Confirm whether formal backcharge notices were issued to Rightway or Quentin Reader; does not block Samtel closeout but affects other trade settlements.

- **Review LamarTech GR list and mark each person remove/keep by end of day** (Whitney, Joseph, Chris)

  Target: 1 senior PM, 1 APM, 1 superintendent; all others removed from burn rate.

- **Build 2-3 page payment strategy deck for ownership** (Joseph, Thomas)

  Show spend to date, remaining balance, monthly payment tranches (Sep-Nov), and resource costs to execute; align with John's framing before finalizing.

- **Finalize and send the Ancora letter template** (John)

  Lightly modified version already drafted; send once trade names are confirmed.

- **Share full lien notice list with Ankura and Todd** (Brandon/Alana)

  Alana to send a fresh copy to the full group.

- **Quantify design errors and omissions exposure** (Whitney, Chris)

  Target to get something out this week; feeds the $25M recovery plan and the ownership presentation.

- Outstanding balance: \~$216k total, with $100k in dispute
- Disputed $100k: McCarthy claims a lump-sum agreement for work performed Nov 4 to May 1 (the “void period” before a true contract was in place)
- McCarthy’s email references LOI #2, citing a $100k lump-sum agreement for that period
- Chuck: KozPure agreed to LOI as “not to exceed,” not a lump sum; any lump-sum agreement was between McCarthy and their own cost team

# LOI #2 Scope and Schematic Deliverable Question

- LOI #2 deliverable was schematic design, contingent on contracting structural, MEP, and other consultants
- Team’s agreed definition: schematics = consultants fully engaged and producing high-level analysis
- Consultants were never formally contracted under McCarthy/Perkins \& Will, so schematics were never entered
- Josh’s signature crossed out “concept” and wrote “schematic” throughout the LOI pages, confirming the intent
- Chuck: McCarthy was tracking percent complete throughout the project per KozPure’s standing request
  - They should have documented data on schematic completion percentage

# Core Dispute Argument

- If schematic completion is 0%, McCarthy should be paid 0% of the \~$404k scope
- Avoids line-item tit-for-tat: payment tied solely to percent of schematic deliverable achieved
- Chuck: billing for 100% of scope with zero work product is the core discrepancy
- Geotech oversight line item: ran directly through KozPure, not McCarthy; likely billable to zero

# Perkins \& Will Invoice Thread

- Separate $100k portion of the invoice relates to Perkins \& Will costs
- Charlie spoke with Don (Sand); Don is checking internally whether payment can be received outside the McCarthy design-build contract path
- Don and Sam understand the situation; their team is working through corporate approval channels
- Whitney to follow up with Don tomorrow, nudging toward an SDs path outside the McCarthy route if they want faster resolution

# Next Steps

- **Reach out to McCarthy to understand schematic completion percentage** (Greg)

  Play it casual: frame as diving into the LOA and wanting to understand what deliverables were completed and what percent of schematics they believe are done.
- **Ask Perkins \& Will separately for their schematic completion percentage**

  Use the team's agreed definition: schematics required consultants fully engaged; ask what deliverables they can point to.

notes.title: SPH x Level Up | Engagement Plan
notes.summary_markdown:
# SPH Project Overview

- Sports Performance Hub: 92-acre complex in Homestead, FL (Exit 2)
- Five sport verticals: soccer, tennis, baseball, basketball, golf (golf offsite, partnership with Leur)
- Key facilities: 5,000-seat stadium, 6 fields (1 natural grass, 5 synthetic), racket complex (clay, hard courts, padel), field house, gymnasium, sports medicine/ambulatory surgery center, dorms, academy school, 150-key hotel, 1,200-space parking
- Boarding academy for up to 600 students
- Site is essentially abandoned land, last developed pre-Hurricane Andrew (30+ years ago)
- All utilities likely need to be run from scratch

# Project Status and Challenges

- Only completed asset: one natural grass baseball field (finished March 2026)
- Stadium currently in DDs; everything else in flux
- Miami FC/USL temporary stadium deal at Harris Field collapsed today, forcing full pivot back to SPH site
- Original $230M budget for the entire complex: widely considered unrealistic given Miami construction costs and escalation
- Phase 1a budget: $23M (fields + some tennis courts + padel + temporary tennis center building)
- Moss Construction engaged informally for high-level ROM estimate only, not contracted for precon
- City of Homestead permitting is a major risk: outsources all reviews, building official quit the week Gabby started
- Board: retired professional athletes and investors with no construction experience, demanding ROI
- No contracts in place with any vendor; everything has been verbal agreements

# Gabby’s Situation and What She Needs

- Joined end of June 2026; has been in reactive mode since, trying to impose structure
- Party of one: no PM, no admin support
- Hiring plan: two people in January (PM + junior admin)
- Immediate need: get fields and some tennis mobilizing this fall; construction should have already started
- Building 2027 budget now: critical timing to forecast Level Up’s support and costs
- Core ask: owner’s rep support to act as filter, build proactive schedules and budgets, and structure board/investor presentations
- Don (Parker’s contact, hired as SPH owner’s rep before Gabby) has not delivered execution; Gabby is actively questioning the relationship
- Gabby’s style: extremely hands-on, hates bottlenecks, makes fast decisions, expects her owner’s rep to be a true extension of ownership

# Parker / Don Dynamic

- Don Moore introduced Level Up to SPH; was hired as SPH owner’s rep before Gabby came on board
- Gabby’s view of Parker: FF\&E procurement specialists (loose furniture, stadium seating, LED, AV/tech), not owner’s rep
- Level Up’s history with Parker: competitive bid wins at Mercedes-Benz Stadium and Jaguars training facility, strictly FF\&E procurement
- Don’s role at Inter Miami: relationship-driven, strong on sales, weak on execution; Level Up had to hold Parker accountable at the loading dock
- Gabby’s concern: funds were allocated for owner’s rep services that have not been rendered; no execution, just meetings
- Parker positioned Level Up to Gabby as “boots on the ground construction guys,” not owner’s rep, which prompted her to set up this call

# Proposal and Next Steps

- Greg to put together a simple, two-option proposal by end of week (scope of services, phased look-ahead, budget/schedule structure)
- Gabby will present to Nick (her boss) this afternoon to get budget approved for 2027
- Level Up’s pitch: lean team (Whitney, Greg, Justin), no corporate overhead, economical pricing, Miami-fluent, private developer mindset
- Relevant Level Up experience cited: Inter Miami (replaced Legends, Icon, JLL), Jaguars (replaced Comcore as owner’s rep after 60 days), Sphere Las Vegas (ongoing)
- Gabby’s expectation: Level Up acts as first line of defense, filters architect/contractor noise, escalates only what needs her attention

# Next Steps

- **Send Gabby a simple proposal with scope of services and phased look-ahead** (Greg)

  Gabby is presenting to Nick this afternoon and building the 2027 budget now; sooner the better.

---

Chat with meeting transcript: [https://notes.granola.ai/t/90abbfa0-512f-4db6-af3a-acdec0fcd4a6](https://notes.granola.ai/t/90abbfa0-512f-4db6-af3a-acdec0fcd4a6)

notes.title: Brock x Whitney | Chat
notes.summary_markdown:
### Brock’s Background

- Georgia Tech business grad (2015), originally engineering
- Interned on the Falcons/Mercedes-Benz Stadium project with Icon (owner’s rep)
  - Stayed on full-time post-grad as APM, overseeing budget, schedule, contractor, architect from dirt to opening
  - Completed master’s in building construction at Georgia Tech (night program) concurrently
- Left for Brasfield \& Gorrie (healthcare, \~2 years), then worked for Dan Cathy on a 25-acre highway-cap park concept in Atlanta
- Rejoined Impact, moved to Jacksonville with Greg to oversee Jaguars training facility and stadium pre-development
- Launched Levelup-pd with Greg; first client was Dan Cathy, then Inter Miami (replacing Icon) from March 2024
  - Opened Inter Miami’s facility April 4, 2026; still on-site for day-two additions

### Levelup-pd: Model and Projects

- Boutique owner’s rep, intentionally small: Brock, Greg, Jordan, and Brock’s brother
  - Target size: \~12 people, up to 3 projects at once
  - Core sell: principals (Brock + Greg) boots-on-ground, not flying in Monday/leaving Thursday
- Sports and entertainment niche only; competes against Icon (massive, doing Chiefs, Broncos, Commanders) and Impact (\~53 people)
- Portfolio: Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Falcons, Jaguars training facility, Porsche HQ/track, Inter Miami stadium
- Active projects:
  - Inter Miami day-two scope (clubs, suite expansions)
  - Sacramento 8,000-seat arena (arena soccer, Sacramento State basketball, ice hockey): hard budget $175M, design currently tracking $250-300M; working to value-engineer scope down
  - DC Sphere (early engagement)
  - Tuesday call on a 10,000-seat stadium with hotel, soccer fields, youth academy, and baseball fields (South Florida/Homestead area)

### Owner’s Rep Work: How It Actually Works

- Engaged as early as possible: strategy, early budgets and schedules, architect procurement, delivery method selection, GMP prep
- Typically brought in after concept phase, around start of real design; architect is often already on board by then
- Pulls owner-direct scopes away from the CM to avoid 3-4% contractor fee (e.g., technology, seating, and on Inter Miami, a $200M superstructure and cable-net roof)
- Sacramento as a case study in first-time developer education:
  - Client wanted 18-month build with 12 pages of drawings: not feasible
  - Built a basic master schedule covering design, permitting, CM procurement, and construction phasing
  - Recommending 100% SD package go to market for CM pricing before full design commitment
  - Perkins \& Will on architecture, McCarthy sidelined until drawings are more advanced, Rogers Civil for traffic/environmental
- Finance background is highly transferable: budget and schedule are where all decisions flow through

### Advice for Whitney and Next Steps

- Best learning comes from being on-site and asking questions constantly, even ones that feel basic
- Finance foundation is an asset: budget and contingency fluency translates directly to owner’s rep work
- Brock offered to share documents and materials to review as they come up (no strings, just to spark curiosity)
- Brock will be in Atlanta in a few weeks; open to grabbing coffee

### Next Steps

- **Meet Brock for coffee when he's in Atlanta**

  Brock will be in Atlanta in a couple of weeks; Whitney to confirm timing.

- **Reach out to Brock when job searching closer to May graduation**

  Brock offered introductions to contacts at firms across both owner's rep and contractor routes.

---

  Include front row depth note; Chandler needs it to assess attic stock and seat type options.

  Jesus targeting mid-week; Chandler will cross-check against existing list.

  - Format will mirror the SNR presentation, cleaned up and made consistent per group
  - 9/14 and 9/21 payment dates discussed; bouncing to Matt for final sign-off before confirming

# Defect Pricing Approach

- Building a spreadsheet with one row per defect, columns for:
  - Hard cost impact (pulled from CO log and CRB log)
  - Revenue loss
  - Operational impact (e.g., additional security, relocated staff, lost C-route revenue)
  - Soft cost/design impact (time, consultant hours)
  - Net total per defect
- Hard costs: running first-pass surges with George to capture subcontractor CO costs incurred
- Markups: flat consistent GC/GR rate applied across all defects (same load as the $622M job)
- Some line items will have real quotes; others will be estimates with backup justification
- Bill and Jose’s time (e.g., railing walk yesterday) to be captured as soft cost
- Brandon Briggs to add operational items: additional labor, lost revenue, etc.

- Key framing from the call: don’t claim the cost of the item itself, claim the delta and the premium

# Meeting Structure and Goals

- Weekly cadence: Tuesday mornings + Thursday 2pm check-ins, plus ad hoc targeted sessions
- 79 vendors in closeout; meetings structured to stay focused and avoid derailment
- Today’s goals: complete vendor status review, confirm documentation tracking process, align on payment strategy and wave schedule

- Need a back-end checklist per trade confirming exactly what closeout docs have been received

# Payment Strategy and Wave Approach

- Two-payment approach: first payment to prompt engagement, second held as leverage
- Ankura pushing for top-down global settlement view vs. Lemar Tech’s pay-app-by-pay-app approach
  - Tension: global settlement better captures back charges, clawbacks, and leverage needs
  - Procore can be configured to support global approach rather than pay-app sequencing

- Ownership expectation: hold a buffer beyond identified recovery total

  - Confirm with SNR/ETS that no pending back charges exist
  - Documentation TBD: shop drawings, mill certs needed; homework before 21st

  - Need to pay \~80–90% (retainage hold), then request pricing for lighting enclosure additions
  - Confirm with architect whether updated ASK was issued too late for fabrication window
  - Targeting first payment wave; Jesus to audit how many planter locations have the blue hose temporary fix
- Custom Doors (frameless FCU closet doors): scope complete, docs provided; two COs under review by Justin/George; recommend Category A and payment
- ESM (hand dryers): scope complete, no back charges; recommend payment; hand dryer install responsibility dispute with Miller to be resolved separately
- Either Works International (pool material): material only, early contract (pre-sales tax exemption); docs need validation; recommend Category A

- CRB items for work not started or not proceeding: use existing “work status” column in master log to tag these; Chris to align with Andres
- Procore tracker: Rodrigo responsible for reconciling all payments in Procore regardless of payment source
- Zero-balance vendors (FPL louvers, ENF Builders, Buyer Response, Jam Industries, Winlock Corp, Pro Bell, EST, Beyond Industrial): all need lien waivers confirmed; Jennifer to verify Jam Industries waivers; Jonathan to check Winlock waivers

# Meeting Cadence and Note-Taking Discipline

- Agreed to publish meeting notes with clear actions and commitments to drive the next meeting
- Running daily log of all Lamar Tech commitments to be maintained and updated continuously
- Thomas to be put on top of ensuring Whitney receives copies of all relevant materials
- Current once-a-week cadence deemed insufficient: need to meet more frequently
  - Next meeting set for Thursday
  - Work session tomorrow, 1:30–4:00 PM

# Budget Baseline: 622 vs. 626

- Lamar Tech circulated a cost summary showing $626M, up from the locked $622M baseline
  - Difference traced largely to Lamar Tech destaffing costs
  - Number cannot keep moving: ownership will lose confidence if the goalpost shifts
- Resolution: lock $622M as the hard baseline; anything new goes below the line (e.g., starting at line 108), dated by week
  - Week of 9/1, week of 9/8, etc., each with their own change rows
  - Lamar Tech to be told to revert to the $622M baseline before this deck goes to ownership

# Closeout Dashboard and Contractor Readiness

- Deck structured around $91M remaining across trade contractors (top 20 = 86% of the money)
  - Slide 1: big picture budget summary leading to the $91M figure
  - Slide 2: closeout tracker dashboard by category
  - Slide 3: contractor readiness breakdown
- Currently 20 contractors in “ready to present” category; could grow if today’s meeting A-ratings are validated
  - Consensus: do not take Lamar Tech’s self-reported A ratings at face value; vet before updating the dashboard
- Key risks flagged:
  - Budget is a moving target: \~$190K+ in change orders may belong to Day 2 operational projects, not this scope
  - Lamar Tech reducing crew, compromising throughput
  - Potential contentious/sour-grapes contractors (e.g., Miller with $11M crawl recovery exposure)

# Contractor Grouping and Settlement Cadence

- Settlement order to be a mix of high and low dollar contractors
  - First batch: prioritize low-hanging fruit to aggressively reduce the count of 79 open contractors
  - Subsequent batches: mix of easy and complex, but follow the established order
- Lamar Tech to be given limited time to flag sequencing concerns by assignee; after that, the order is fixed
- Two-stage payment structure:
  - Stage 1: initial payment sufficient to bring contractor back to finish and deliver paperwork
  - Stage 2: reserve held until audit closes, crawl recovery resolved, punch list complete
- Frag to be moved to Group A (early payment): minimal disputes, partner relationship

# Crawl Analysis and Payment Framing

- Crawl ran up significant costs; working to flatten the payment cycle and re-engage them
- Chase (Crawl) to provide a breakdown of the \~$1M spend across audits and deep dives
  - Goal: map spend to recoverable savings (e.g., $200K here → $3M recoverable) to justify invoices to ownership
- Lamar Tech’s payment recommendation (\~$20M+) to be socialized against the team’s own analysis
  - Their view is pay-up-to-pay; team’s view is global settlement: need to reconcile
- Retainage definition needs to be locked down: the $20M figure is not real as currently stated

# Amp Think and “Others” Line Item

- Amp Think costs currently buried in the “Others” category alongside tariffs and freight
- Need a clear breakdown of total Amp Think cost:
  - LED costs
  - Speaker costs
  - ZDI cost (allocated to the GR)
- Ensure the total is visible somewhere in the deck so ownership can ask and get a clean answer

# Outreach to Trade Contractors and Next Steps

- Todd email drafted with framing for 2–3 outreach emails to trades
  - Granola/team to add detail on checklist expectations and close-out requirements
  - Todd to review for legal/CIA considerations; target: send tomorrow
  - Blanket email to all trades to mention that individual contractor checklists will follow
- Call with Todd to be set for tomorrow afternoon
- Deck to be the single source of truth for ownership: Lamar Tech’s piecemeal outputs should not go directly to the brothers
- Mid-September and end-of-September milestones to be added to the deck before it goes out
- October 2026 closeout target flagged as ambitious: may be worth communicating this to ownership to reset expectations

# Next Steps

- **Lock budget baseline at $622M and restructure tracker**

  All new items go below the line, dated by week; Lamar Tech to be told to revert before deck is issued to anyone.
- **Reconcile Procore and Lamar Tech tracker numbers** (Whitney, Thomas, Joseph)

  Work session tomorrow 1:30–4:00 PM; flag any change orders not properly captured, especially drawer-find COs.
- **Establish payment ranges for Stage 1 and Stage 2** (Whitney, Thomas)

  Target a solid draft by end of tomorrow; feeds the cash flow slide and overall settlement strategy.
- **Request Lamar Tech staffing plan with committed hours**

  Send email now; plan must name people and hours, not just headcount, to prevent "not enough resources" excuses later.
- **Finalize and send trade contractor outreach emails**

  Add checklist detail and flavor; Todd to review for legal sign-off; target send tomorrow.
- **Add mid-September and end-of-September milestones to the deck**

-   Wholesale masks dashboard built to answer Graham’s current questions
-   Scope: $5.21M across 79 contractors, broken down by vendor
-   Excludes Lemartech, customs, and duties from this view
-   Retainage figure (~$28M) flagged as likely misleading
    -   Includes “to be retained” amounts on unpaid invoices, not just held retainage
    -   Real held retainage estimated closer to $25M

### Slide Structure (Work in Progress)

-   Slide 1: Contractual breakdown by contractor (the “story in numbers” for senior execs)
    -   Top 20 vendors = 85-86% of the $91M
    -   Bottom 60 contractors make up the remainder
-   Slide 2: Closeout tracker dashboard showing review progress by category (complete, in progress, started)
    -   SIP and sales tax being moved to a separate bucket, not blocking stage one payments
-   Slide 3: Contractor readiness groupings (A/B/C or 1/2/3/4/5 tiers)
    -   20 of 79 contractors currently in “ready to present” column, representing $5.6M of $91M
-   Slide 4: Anticipated cash flow, based on least aggressive of three internal scenarios
    -   Needs to be vetted by Lemartech as construction manager before publishing
    -   Caveat to be added that criteria are preliminary

### Payment Structure

-   Two-payment model per vendor being tracked
    -   Stage one: partial payment now, leaving a reserve for leverage
    -   Stage two: final payment after closeout items resolved (SIP, sales tax, etc.)
-   Three cash flow scenarios developed internally; lowest/least aggressive shown in dashboard
    -   Logic: better to undershoot and pay more later than to overpromise

### Grouping Tiers and Readiness Review

-   Internal disagreement on criteria for what makes a contractor a 1 vs. 2 vs. 3 (or A/B/C)
-   “1” and “A” are equivalent; ones assigned in last Tuesday’s session should all map to A
-   Remaining tier assignments still need to be decided collaboratively
-   Whitney wants to review and align on the 20 “ready to present” contractors before locking in

### Next Steps

-   **Review and align on the 20 "ready to present" contractors** (Whitney)
    
    Confirm the list jointly before it's locked into the dashboard.
    
-   **Agree on A/B/C/D (or 1/2/3/4/5) tier criteria and assignments**
    
    Internal divergence on criteria needs resolution before stage one payment thresholds can be set.
    
-   **Vet cash flow scenarios with Lemartech**
    
    Construction manager sign-off needed before the cash flow slide is shared with Graham or Jose Mas.
    
-   **Add Incur and Levelup attribution to the relevant dashboard slide**
    
    Whitney suggested crediting both firms to reflect their visibility into the data.

notes.title: Level Up x SRK
notes.summary_markdown:
# SRK Strategies Introduction

- Brooklyn-based PR agency specializing in sports and sports-adjacent clients
- Sarah Starks and Leah Orlando both work across the Rancho Cordova account
- Goal: announce the Level Up x Rancho Cordova partnership via press release

# Level Up Background (for PR Context)

- Whitney and Greg are owners of Level Up
- 20+ years in sports development and mixed-use development
- Most recent project: Miami Freedom Park Stadium (Inter Miami, MLS)
- Role is “owner’s rep”: managing design teams, engineers, contractors, third parties, entitlements, city/building departments
- Prior firm: CAA Icon (reference point for SRK to understand scope)
- Notable past projects: Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta Falcons, Jacksonville Jaguars, $3B mixed-use including stadium, training facility, Four Seasons hotel, Porsche HQ expansion

# Press Release Approach

- SRK will draft first; Level Up to review and approve before pitching
- Key inputs needed:
  - Level Up boilerplate or a previous press release they liked
  - A deck (Josh/Charlie mentioned one may exist)
  - Photos: professional job site shots and candid on-site images available
- Quote strategy:
  - SRK will draft a few quote options for Whitney and/or Greg to choose from
  - Tone: belief in the client and vision, excitement for the partnership, what Level Up hopes to bring to Rancho Cordova
  - Community angle: stadiums as civic anchors, not just sports venues; Level Up’s nomadic lifestyle (5 cities in 7 years) as a “we make the project our home” narrative
- Possible future releases to consider:
  - Perkins \& Will (architect, Don Dethlefs noted as a leading voice in mid-size 6,000-8,000 capacity arenas)
  - General contractor announcement (contractor selection upcoming)
  - Releases can be packaged together or spaced \~3 weeks apart for sustained momentum

# Media and Interviews

- Focus is local news
- Whitney and Greg open to interviews (panels, sit-downs, etc.)
- SRK will prep them fully; this call was treated as informal/internal

# Next Steps

- **Send Level Up boilerplate and/or a prior press release to SRK** (Whitney, Greg)

  SRK will use it as a foundation for the first draft.
- **Share the Level Up deck and job site photos with SRK** (Whitney, Greg)

  Both professional and candid images welcome to accompany the release.
- **SRK to deliver first press release draft by mid-September** (Sarah, Leah)

  Target is right after Labor Day; Level Up to review and approve before any pitching.

---

notes.title: DOVA | P&W Interim Agreement Chat
notes.summary_markdown:
# Meeting Purpose

- Quick scan of DOVA interim agreement markups from Jason Palmer (Cosper’s legal)
- Goal: get the interim agreement signed with minimal changes, push heavy negotiation to the B-133

# General Stance on Markups

- Most of Jason’s changes are unnecessary rewrites, reordering, or minor language tweaks
- Recommendation: revert to clean version with only minor agreed modifications
- Exhibit A: leave as is, no sticking points
- Exhibit B: cannot accept Jason’s changes without lawyers involved
  - Warranties, “good faith” language, insurance amounts, stripped liability protections for architect
  - Any changes to Exhibit B require legal-to-legal conversation

# Agreed Minor Edits (No Legal Needed)

- Update seat count (consistent with contract count)
- Change header to read “Attention: Charlie and Josh” instead of current format
- Fee figure: $1,715,970 vs. $1,715,972 (likely rounding from waterfall calc), can be corrected

# Key Sticking Point: Instruments of Service / Ownership

- Jason’s markups imply Cosper could terminate and receive all working models and in-progress files
- Sam’s team reads this as: “terminate at end of SD, then hand off everything to a different architect”
- Perkins Will’s position:
  - SD deliverable PDF is what the client gets at end of SD
  - Revit models and in-progress working files are not deliverable upon termination
  - Willing to accept language limited to “in-process PDF deliverables”
- Agreed: ownership of models deferred entirely to B-133 negotiation
- Termination language (10 business days notice) is acceptable; the additive ownership clause is not

# Next Steps

- **Call Jason Palmer to revert interim agreement to clean version** (Whitney)

  Allow only the minor agreed edits: seat count, header, fee rounding, and softened ownership language referencing PDF deliverables only.
- **Send Sam a summary email and clean draft for quick review** (Whitney)

  Confirm no changes slipped through that would require legal review before Charlie signs.
- **Email Charlie summarizing the outcome** (Whitney)

  Note that ownership language is deferred to B-133, and that Cosper owns the SD deliverable PDF upon termination, not working models.

---

notes.title: Contractor closeout strategy — payment, recovery, and sequencing with Joseph
notes.summary_markdown:
# Closeout Strategy Overview

- Goal: move from planning to execution on subcontractor closeouts
- Approach: tiered groupings (A/B/C/D) by complexity and readiness
  - Group A: clean checklist, easy wins, get them out the door
  - Group B: some substance, need to review change orders and punch list before meeting
  - Group C/D: complex, large dollar, more challenging negotiations
- Miller and PO-type groups treated separately from the main process
- Target closeout: end of October, with some bleed into November
- Priority lane concept: for every hard sub, close two or three easy ones in parallel

# Internal Pre-Meeting Process (Before Engaging Subs)

- Internal alignment meeting required before any external outreach
  - Confirm disputed change orders with full team (Anthony, Rodrigo, etc.)
  - Align on back charges, punch list credits, and recoverable amounts
  - Validate nothing is missing from Le-Martech’s perspective
- Each sub to have a closeout binder with:
  - Document submission checklist (submitted / approved / pending)
  - Back charge log
  - Punch list valuation
  - Sales tax and LSIP adjustments
  - Change order categorization: new stadium (622M budget) vs. post-opening improvements

# External Engagement Process

- Initial outreach: communicate payment plan and closeout expectations to subs
  - Whitney (and John when back) leading all external correspondence
  - Message: here’s your initial payment, here’s the closeout checklist, here’s your target meeting date (\~3 weeks out)
- Payment strategy: make a minimum initial payment to each sub that:
  - Keeps enough leverage for punch list, back charges, and recovery
  - Gets subs re-engaged (many stalled because unpaid)
- Goal this week: SNR payment schedule for critical subs, some payments out by end of week
- Firm meeting dates to be set by end of week (Zoom, Teams, or in-person)

# Avenues of Recovery (Per Sub)

- Back charges: cleaning allocation exercise complete (Lorenzo de Fabriz); splits subs into charged/not charged
- LSIP adjustments: CR Solutions engaged, results expected soon
- Sales tax: tracked by Le-Martech
- Punch list: \~1,400 items total
  - \~1,200 tiling-related (bulk)
  - \~200 spread across other trades
  - High-importance items: pushed to subs to fix
  - Low-importance items: valued and back-charged for diminished value
- Change order clawback: CO audit underway, categorizing by new stadium vs. post-opening
- Tariff credits: run a search across all contracts for tariff language; some tariffs may have been repealed, credits should flow back

# JJ’s (Doors / Hardware)

- Not returning to site; punch list items accumulating and risk of “not our damage” claims grows over time
- Crawl estimated \~$400–500K recoverable; no backup data provided yet
- CRB: \~$512K in pending change orders, mostly work already performed but not yet approved
- Recommended initial payment: February draw (\~$233K)
- Remaining balance after payment: \~$475K (inflated by CRB); effective remaining scope \~$75K
- Target incremental recovery: \~$250K (soft circle)
- Action: get Crawl backup data for their recovery estimate; clarify CRB breakdown (performed vs. not performed)

# Baker

- Crawl estimated \~$5M recovery potential; team flagged significant contract impediments
  - Contract language: every change order is “final settlement” for matters contained, limiting ability to reopen
  - Several large change orders show rounded settlement values (e.g., $700K), suggesting prior commercial negotiation
  - Lump sum contract: contractor cannot claim more for quantity variances
- Council already engaged to assess whether Crawl’s recovery avenues are viable
- Internal assessment document drafted (similar to DCL pamphlet format); for internal use only before presenting to ownership or subs

# LTG (Landscaping / Irrigation)

- \~$456K acceleration change order disputed; team recommends rejection
  - LTG finished in \~6 weeks vs. 12-week original schedule, but did not work double shifts as change order specified
  - Counter-argument: they mobilized 47 people vs. 12 committed, and delivered on time
  - Strategy: negotiate a global settlement rather than full rejection; propose paying \~60% and settling holistically
- Additional disputed items:
  - 6-inch LRP irrigation work (\~$136K): only \~6–7 inches of fill needed, not the 1 foot claimed; labor only, no material
  - Additional irrigation work (\~$42K): scope already included in original contract; pressure testing charge also disputed
- LTG essentially complete; no punch list work needed from them
- Procore bulk download access needed to efficiently pull all change order data

# Alpha Cladding (Glazing)

- Submitted \~$1M overtime change order with weekly payroll backup; not in CRB
- Previously paid $480K in acceleration; team questions whether that spend was legitimate
  - Math check: $480K at $65.50/hr with 47 guys = implausible hours
- Root cause analysis started: dry-in milestone delays traced to late glass delivery and framing not ready
  - West side steel was \~6 weeks behind original schedule
  - Field suites glass delayed by shoring/reshoring issues and lack of buck hoist
  - Team acknowledges some owner-side coordination failures
- Glass not yet tested; no warranties submitted; accordion glass installation direction may have been changed via email (need to locate that email)
- Strategy: finish schedule delay analysis before responding to the $1M claim

# Action Items

- **Send Procore access request email** (Joseph)

  Need correspondence tool access and bulk download capability for change order data; spoken to Lorenzo but formal email not yet sent.
- **Finalize sub groupings (A/B/C/D) and initial payment amounts**

  Target end of this week; feeds ownership dashboard and payment schedule for critical subs.
- **Draft and send initial payment communications to subs** (Whitney)

  Include payment amount, closeout checklist, and soft-circled meeting date \~3 weeks out.
- **Get Crawl backup data for JJ's recovery estimate**

  Crawl cited \~$400–500K recoverable but no supporting data has been provided.
- **Add dollar values to all blank recoverable columns in tracker** (Jordan, team)

  Any unknown amounts to be sent to Crawl for valuation; LTG's $456K and others need populated values before budget can move.
- **Run contract search for tariff language across all subs**

  Some tariffs may have been repealed; any credits owed should flow back to ownership.
- **Locate email authorizing accordion glass installation direction change**

  Alleged Eric Wine email; no one has seen it and it represents a major design deviation on Alpha Cladding scope.
- **Build simplified ownership dashboard from tracker** (Whitney)

  High-level view showing progress and indicative recovery (high/low range); updated 2–3x per week.

---

notes.title: Kroll Meeting
notes.summary_markdown:
# Kroll Team Introductions

- Chase’s group specializes in construction expert services
  - Chase: 15+ years, \~200 disputes, testified \~20 times (state courts, arbitrations, US/Canada)
  - Taylor: quantity surveyor, trained in the UK, led change order review
- John Byrne (Ankar): civil engineer, large capital project delivery, testified \~20 times
- Joseph Regara: delay and quantum analysis, local Miami resource, 24 years in construction
- Thomas Ward: advisory projects at Ankar, Philadelphia office, 3 years

# Change Order Review Scope and Methodology

- \~$60M in changes reviewed across 19-20 subcontractors
  - Biggest targets: Baker Concrete, Qualico Steel, Miller Electric
- General approach per subcontractor:
  - Reviewed contract, drawings, and scope to assess legitimacy of changes
  - BIM model quantity takeoffs compared against contracted vs. installed quantities
  - Checked rates for reasonableness against trade agreement
  - Mini delay analyses for acceleration/scheduling claims
  - Back charges explored throughout (responsibility between trades)
- Full Procore access used: drawings, RFIs, submittals, all revisions
- Collaborative process with Whitney, Chris, and Andrew over several months of weekly meetings

# Baker Concrete Deep Dive

- Original PO: $51M; approved change orders: $9M; pending: $500K; CRB: $1.7M
  - New contract value if all approved: $63M
- BIM quantity comparison:
  - Baker contracted + approved COs: 45,000 CY concrete
  - BIM model actual: 38,000 CY
  - Surplus of \~7,000 CY, translating to \~$5M potential savings (line 5)
  - Additional miscellaneous adjustments: \~$300K (line 6)
  - Potential final value if savings realized: \~$57M
- Rates in change orders are neat-line CY but include wastage in quantity buildups
  - Rates vary across COs; average rate approach used as most practical method
- Building G retail wing flagged as unresolved issue
  - Baker’s argument: cross-hatched scope marked “not completed,” so they carried zero
  - Counter-argument: Baker knew the building existed and should have carried an allowance
  - Change order for Building G not yet reviewed; expected to be a large number

# Procore Workflow and Change Order Status Definitions

- Three stages in Procore:
  1. CRB (Change Review Board): Lamar Tech completes review, presents to ownership
  2. Pending (CCO): approved in CRB, not yet fully executed via DocuSign
  3. Approved: fully executed, backup loaded into Procore
- Voided CCOs: some were pulled back after CRB approval; appear as “void” in commitment change order log

# Tracker, Document Sharing, and Next Steps

- Level Up internal tracker covers all subs:
  - CO audit status (not started / in progress / input needed / complete)
  - Potential audit recovery and back charges by trade
  - Design-driven change order tagging feeding a running total
  - Punch list, defective work, lien documentation, LD assessment, sales tax credits
- Kroll to create a mirrored Titan file for John’s team with all relevant backup
  - Decks for Baker, Qualico, Glen Reader, and others to be uploaded/confirmed in Titan
  - Some internal spreadsheets need tidying before sharing
- Focus for the near term: three subcontractors where Kroll has completed the bulk of analysis
  - Goal is targeted, narrow follow-up questions, not a full re-investigation
- Negotiation timeline: “sooner rather than later”; short and long timeframes being finalized with Graham next week

# Next Steps

- **Share Kroll backup files and decks via Titan**

  Baker, Qualico, Glen Reader, and others; Kroll to tidy internal spreadsheets and upload or confirm already in Titan.
- **Review Baker's Building G change order in Procore**

  Confirm what Baker carried (or didn't) for the retail wing scope vs. what should have been in their original buyout.
- **Schedule mid-week check-in to review progress**

  Target week of 17th August; gives the team time to absorb Kroll's work product before sub negotiations begin.
- **Share sub negotiation timetable once finalized**

  Plan being developed with Graham; Kroll needs timing to plan their support role.

---

notes.title: Stadium project — change order closeout and contractor settlement strategy with John
notes.summary_markdown:
# Project Background and Team Setup

- Chris brought in as in-house construction lead, relocated from Texas
- Decision made to go with Lamarck as CM; acknowledged as a known limitation the team is managing around
- John introduced as consultant: 15+ years running work for GCs and owners, heavy civil and power background, now focused on project closeout and settlement negotiation
- Whitney and Level Up team provide bid process expertise; Chris holds the strongest pulse on post-groundbreak execution

# Change Order Process Failures

- Fast-track stadium project with immovable deadline meant no time for proper CO review, negotiation, or documentation
- Lamarck received COs from trades months before presenting to ownership, then used urgency (“we need this to keep work going”) to force approvals
- COs submitted piecemeal by trade, not packaged by change event
  - A single design change affecting 7 divisions would arrive as 7 separate COs weeks or months apart
  - No way to assess full cost impact of any one change event in real time
- Audit language added to approvals once the pattern was recognized, but only after significant damage
- Lamarck’s internal Change Review Board (CRB) process existed but was poorly executed
  - CRBs sometimes took months to generate before hitting ownership’s desk
  - Whitney and Chris routinely found holes in submissions within seconds, sending them back repeatedly
- Ownership will likely be accused of slow CO approval; trades couldn’t bill or release materials for extended periods
- Crawl conducted analysis but approach was validating (checking findings against correspondence) rather than fortifying (building a position from evidence)
  - Miller reviewed Crawl’s findings; didn’t reject outright but offered $1.3M-$2.5M reduction vs. the $8M proposed
  - Ownership’s current stance: $2-2.5M is a no-go starting point

# Contractor Status and Settlement Strategy

- Most trades substantially complete; minor punch list items remain
- Largest incomplete scope: Glen Reader (owes 88 lux units, not performing due to non-payment since January)
  - Several trades unpaid since February or March; payment delinquency is the primary reason for punch list stalls
  - Only one month during the project did ownership pay trades on time
- Venera threatened with descope over elevator/camera/controls work; resolved after pressure, mobilizing tomorrow
- A1 has 1,500 punch items, only 10% complete as of last Friday
- John’s near-term priorities:
  - Get into Procore over the weekend to review documents in depth
  - Meet with Crawl to walk through their analysis and supporting documents
  - Have informed conversation with counsel early next week
  - Identify which contracts to move on first and begin signaling seriousness to trades
  - Two additional team members joining Thursday/Friday to support
- Settlement approach: offer measured pre-settlement payments to get trades to the table, but calibrate carefully to preserve leverage

# Next Steps

- **Grant John access to Procore**

  John needs to review correspondence and CRB records before counsel meeting early next week.
- **Schedule working session with John to review documents and get him up to speed**

  John is in town through next week; needs deep-dive beyond what a phone call can cover.
- **Coordinate Crawl walkthrough with John**

  John wants Crawl to walk him through their analysis and documents, ideally over the weekend.

---

notes.title: Site work scope and civil services budget with contractor
notes.summary_markdown:
### Site Work and Earthwork Scope

- Earthwork covers grading for the entire site
- Surface improvements scoped to the hatched area plus three streets: Trade Center, unnamed road, and Kilgore
  - Includes street signs, striping, curb and gutter
- Sanitary sewer, storm drainage, and domestic water scoped to smaller initial buildout
  - Expectation that scope expands as the district grows
- Street lights and landscape limited to hatched area and adjacent streets/sidewalks

### Off-Site Improvements

- Trade Center off-site: sidewalk and curb/gutter along Tristan Drive and Kilgore
- Separate additional page covers true off-site traffic improvements (highways, signage further from site)
  - These are distinct from on-site costs; not banking on city covering them

### Civil Services Budget and Scope Gaps

- Four agreements on file covering traffic, landscape, and early civil work; total \~$920K in costs identified
- \~$600-700K voiced/contracted so far; \~$200K remainder unaccounted for
- Key open question: does the remaining budget carry the project through full CDs, CA, and completed civil and landscape documents, or are additional agreements needed?
- $100K feels low as a buffer; concern about a budget gap surfacing in 3 months when scope is fully expended

- **Send grading/earthwork docket to Whitney**

  Contractor to forward the file; Whitney may not have it in her records.

# Meeting Purpose and Context

- Sync before a broader meeting with the “dova/golden team” to align on agenda and next steps
- Goal: get internal team in sync first, then run a structured education-style meeting with the external group
- Phase 1 arena focus confirmed for the project

# Proposed Agenda for External Meeting

- ISP coordination and communication
  - Walk the team and concert team through who’s been reaching out
  - Offer to take on ISP conversations on their behalf via observational letter
- DASZ structure overview
  - Cover structure, rationale, cost, and when cost offsets via revenue or sponsorship
- Key schedule milestones
  - No CM on board yet; contractor being brought on, SDs design still in progress
  - Target completion: March 2028 (acknowledged as a stretch)
  - High-level milestones needed: carrier engagement timing, ISP group outreach windows
- Anchor tenant/interest requirements
  - As map team and CM ramp up, flag what needs to be called out
- Sponsor and partnership strategy

# Budget and Scope Updates

- Ceiling ID / halo board item cut from scope (easy cut given current budget constraints)
  - Could be revisited if capital grows by \~$100M
- Team is over-budget; cuts were necessary
- IRU rights: Charlie indicated they want to maintain IRU rights (exact definition of IRU unclear)

# Funding, Financing, and External Outreach

- Krista’s team interested in long-term lease financing
- Josh’s team currently more focused on DASZ integration and CNS support, less on ancillary financing
- Johnson (MosTech) reached out to Josh (Thursday or Friday) with potential investor support, pitched in Miami
  - Unclear if Johnson is affiliated with Aztec or separate
- Team not fully looped into all funding needs
- DASZ build cost discussion needed: what the team is responsible for vs. what can be recovered from carriers
- Competitive procurement question expected: how they’re procuring DASZ and convergent network pieces (Wi-Fi, carriers)

  Ask attendees what they want added to the discussion list before the external meeting.
